# 146. Serialization Cache

Generated serializers may cache schema metadata.

The hot path should not repeatedly rebuild schema descriptors.

---

# 147. Compile-Time Encoding

For fixed structures, the compiler can generate direct code:

```text
load field
encode field
store bytes
```

without virtual dispatch.

---

# 148. Branch Reduction

Generated serializers should specialize based on:

- optional presence
- fixed length
- alignment
- schema version.

---

# 149. SIMD

The implementation may use SIMD for:

- byte copying
- checksum
- UTF-8 validation
- primitive conversion

where supported.

---

# 150. CPU Architecture

Generated serialization must support:

```text
x86-64
ARM64
WASM
```

and future architectures through backend lowering.

---

# 151. GPU Boundary

Serialization is primarily CPU work.

GPU serialization may be added later for:

- tensor formats
- bulk datasets
- GPU-native storage

but is not required in 612 core.

---

# 152. Resource Accounting

Serialization tracks:

```text
bytes encoded
bytes decoded
allocations
decode depth
persistent pages
WAL bytes
cache bytes
snapshot bytes
```

through BOOTSTRAP-606.

---

# 153. Quotas

Structured storage quotas include:

```text
max_database_size
max_record_size
max_wal_size
max_page_cache
max_transaction_size
max_snapshot_size
```

---

# 154. Backpressure

Large serialization streams must support:

```text
await encoder.write(...)
```

rather than buffering unlimited data.

---

# 155. Cancellation

Encoding/decoding streams must support cancellation.

A partially decoded object is never returned as valid.

---

# 156. Deterministic Ordering

Canonical maps, sets, schemas, and metadata use deterministic ordering.

This is required for reproducible hashes.

---

# 157. Hashing

The runtime may expose:

```axiom
hash_encoded(value)
```

which hashes canonical AXBIN bytes.

---

# 158. Equality

Serialized equality and semantic equality are distinct.

Two semantically equivalent values may have different encodings if the schema explicitly permits noncanonical encoding.

Canonical mode removes this ambiguity.

---

# 159. Content Addressing

A content-addressed store can use:

```text
ObjectId = Hash(canonical AXBIN)
```

This is a higher-level feature built from 612 + 611.

---

# 160. Deduplication

Persistent storage may deduplicate identical immutable blobs.

Deduplication must not compromise transactional correctness.

---

# 161. Blob Storage

Large values should be stored as blobs rather than forcing them into one page.

Example:

```text
Record
 ↓
BlobId
 ↓
Blob segments
```

---

# 162. Inline Threshold

Small blobs may be stored inline.

Example policy:

```text
<= 4 KiB → inline
> 4 KiB → blob
```

The threshold is configurable.

---

# 163. Large Object Streaming

Large blobs must support streaming read/write without requiring full-memory allocation.

---

# 164. Blob Integrity

Blob segments may contain:

```text
segment ID
offset
length
checksum
```

---

# 165. Garbage Collection of Storage

Persistent storage may require **storage reclamation**, but this is not language garbage collection.

It operates on:

```text
unreachable pages
orphaned blobs
old snapshots
obsolete WAL
```

and is explicit/background controlled.

---

# 166. No Language GC Dependency

Axiom's memory model remains independent of persistent storage reclamation.

This distinction is mandatory.

---

# 167. Compaction

Storage compaction can reclaim fragmented pages.

Policies:

```text
Manual
Background
PressureTriggered
Startup
```

---

# 168. Compaction Resource Limits

Compaction must obey:

- CPU budget
- I/O budget
- memory budget
- storage quota.

---

# 169. Online Compaction

The preferred design allows readers to continue during compaction when possible.

The first implementation may temporarily restrict writers.

---

# 170. Crash During Compaction

Compaction must use:

```text
temporary generation
+
atomic root switch
```

or WAL equivalent.

A crash must leave either the old or new valid state.

---

# 171. Database Format Version

Every persistent store begins with:

```text
magic
format_version
schema_version
page_size
flags
```

# 172. Store Header

```text
generation
```

Preferred migration:

```text
DecodeError

DepthExceeded
AllocationLimit
```

```text
path
```

# 183. No Secret Leakage

If a failed field is marked `@secret`, error diagnostics must not print its contents.

# 184. Compiler Diagnostics

Compiler errors should catch:

- duplicate field IDs
- duplicate variant IDs
- unsupported persistent type
- architecture-dependent persistent type
- incompatible schema evolution
- missing serializer
- recursive schema without indirection
- noncanonical map key
- invalid default.

# 185. Recursive Types

Recursive persistent types require indirection:

```axiom
struct Node {
    value: u64
    next: ObjectId<Node>?

```

A direct infinitely-sized recursive struct is rejected.

---

# 186. Object Graphs

Arbitrary pointer graphs are not serialized automatically.

They must use explicit IDs.

This prevents hidden pointer traversal and accidental huge object graphs.

---

# 187. Stable IDs

Applications can define:

```axiom
@key
```

# 188. Generated Primary Index

The compiler may generate:

```text
UserById
```

without runtime reflection.

# 189. Generated Secondary Index

Example:

generates an index implementation.

# 190. Index Key Encoding

Index keys use canonical AXBIN encoding.

# 191. Composite Keys

Example:

```text
(country, city, user_id)
```

must encode unambiguously.

Length/tag boundaries prevent:

```text
("ab","c")
```

from colliding with:

```text
("a","bc")
```

---

# 192. Prefix Scans

Ordered composite indexes support prefix queries where their encoding permits it.

---

# 193. Query Boundary

612 provides:

```text
get
scan
lookup
range
```

but not SQL.

---

# 194. Query Planner Boundary

Query planning belongs to a later database layer.

# 195. Embedded Database Boundary

The built-in `KvStore` and persistent collections are intentionally modest.

A future full database engine can build on:

```text
PageStore
WAL
Transactions
Indexes
Serializer
```

# 196. No Mandatory Database Dependency

An ordinary Axiom executable using only structs and files must not link:


unless database APIs are referenced.

# 197. Dead Stripping

Unused components are removable:

```text
AXBIN
Schema
WAL
BTree
KV
PersistentMap
```

independently.

# 198. Runtime Profiles

Minimal:

Conceptual operations:

```text
deserialize.field
```

# 200. Compiler Optimization

The compiler may:

- inline scalar encoders
- eliminate redundant copies
- specialize fixed arrays
- fuse encode operations
- eliminate temporary buffers
- vectorize byte copying
- specialize schema versions.

---

# 201. Copy Elimination

Example:

```text
struct
 ↓
temporary buffer
 ↓
encoder
```

may become:

```text
struct
 ↓
encoder
 ↓
output
```

when the destination permits direct writes.

---

# 202. Decoder Optimization

If input is trusted and validated, the compiler may use specialized fast paths.

Untrusted input must retain bounds checks.

---

# 203. Trusted Data

A decoder may be marked:

```axiom
DecodeMode.Trusted
```

only with explicit authority.

Trusted mode must still preserve memory safety.

---

# 204. Security Rule

`Trusted` does not mean:

```text
unsafe
```

It means the caller accepts stronger input assumptions.

---

# 205. IPC Schema Validation

IPC schemas should be validated before accepting a connection payload.

Unknown schema IDs should produce a protocol error rather than attempting arbitrary interpretation.

---

# 206. Network Schema Negotiation

A future protocol layer may negotiate:

```text
SchemaId
Version
Encoding
Compression
```

612 only provides the metadata needed.

---

# 207. Persistent Schema Registry

A store may contain a local schema registry:

```text
SchemaId
 ↓
SchemaDescriptor
```

This enables introspection without runtime reflection of application objects.

---

# 208. Schema Registry Security

Schema descriptors are data, not executable code.

Loading a schema must never execute migration code automatically.

---

# 209. Schema Cache

Schema descriptors can be cached in memory.

Cache eviction does not affect correctness.

---

# 210. Deterministic Schema Fingerprint

Equivalent schema descriptors must produce identical fingerprints.

Source formatting must not affect the fingerprint.

---

# 211. Source Independence

Renaming a source-level type without changing persistent identity can preserve the same schema ID.

Persistent identity is explicit.

---

# 212. Persistent Type Identity

Example:

```axiom
@schema("com.example.User")
struct User { ... }
```

This identity becomes stable across source refactoring.

---

# 213. Namespace

Schema identity should include namespace:

```text
organization.application.type
```

to reduce collisions.

---

# 214. Reserved IDs

Field and variant IDs may reserve ranges for future versions.

---

# 215. Deprecation

Fields can be:

```axiom
@deprecated
```

without removing their IDs.

The ID remains reserved.

---

# 216. Unknown Field Preservation Mode

For proxy systems:

```axiom
Decoder.PreserveUnknown
```

stores raw unknown fields.

The preserved bytes can later be emitted without understanding them.

---

# 217. Canonical Unknown Fields

When re-encoding preserved fields, their original canonical byte sequence should be retained when valid.

---

# 218. Schema Translation

A translation layer can convert:

```text
Schema A
→
Schema B
```

without decoding into a full object graph.

This is useful for gateways.

---

# 219. Streaming Translation

Large messages can be transformed field-by-field.

This minimizes memory.

---

# 220. Persistent Log + Schema

Each log segment stores schema IDs per record or segment.

Schema changes do not require rewriting old records.

---

# 221. Event Sourcing Boundary

Axiom can implement event sourcing using:

```text
PersistentLog
+
Schema
+
Snapshot
```

but event-sourcing semantics remain application-level.

---

# 222. Audit Log

The same primitives can build append-only audit logs.

Security-sensitive audit logs should use integrity/authentication from 610.

---

# 223. Deterministic Replay

A serialized event stream can be replayed using:

```text
schema
+
sequence
+
payload
```

provided application code itself is deterministic.

---

# 224. Persistent Queue

A durable queue can use:

```text
PersistentLog
+
consumer offset
+
transaction
```

The queue layer is above 612.

---

# 225. Storage Transactions + IPC

A service may receive:

```text
request
```

then atomically:

```text
process request
↓
write response state
↓
commit
```

before acknowledging the request.

This provides a foundation for durable services.

---

# 226. Exactly-Once Boundary

612 must not claim distributed exactly-once semantics.

It can provide:

```text
local durable commit
```

only.

Exactly-once across processes/networks requires higher-level protocol design.

---

# 227. Durability Modes

Structured storage exposes:

```text
MemoryOnly
Buffered
Durable
Synchronous
```

Applications select the tradeoff.

---

# 228. MemoryOnly

Useful for tests and caches.

No persistence guarantee.

---

# 229. Buffered

Writes may remain in OS/runtime buffers.

Fast but not power-loss durable.

---

# 230. Durable

Commit waits for the configured storage durability boundary.

---

# 231. Synchronous

Each mutation may force durability immediately.

Useful for critical records but potentially slower.

---

# 232. Group Commit

Multiple transactions can share one durability barrier.

Example:

```text
Tx1
Tx2
Tx3
 ↓
single WAL sync
```

This improves throughput while preserving documented commit semantics.

---

# 233. Commit Ordering

Commit generations are monotonic.

A later generation cannot become durable before required earlier WAL state.

---

# 234. Resource Governor + WAL

WAL growth is quota-controlled.

When the WAL approaches its limit:

```text
checkpoint
↓
compact
↓
reject
```

according to policy.

---

# 235. Storage Pressure

Under low disk space:

1. evict cache
2. compact obsolete storage
3. remove disposable temporary data
4. report pressure
5. reject nonessential writes

The runtime must never delete durable application data automatically.

---

# 236. Cache Classification

Every persistent object is classified:

```text
Durable
Disposable
Temporary
Recoverable
```

Automatic cleanup applies only to disposable/temporary data.

---

# 237. Backup Boundary

612 can expose:

```text
snapshot()
export()
```

but backup transport belongs to a higher layer.

---

# 238. Export

A store can export a consistent snapshot:

```text
snapshot generation
+
schema
+
records
```

without stopping readers.

---

# 239. Import

Import must validate:

- format
- schema
- checksums
- bounds
- quotas

before activation.

---

# 240. Atomic Activation

Imported data becomes active through:

```text
new generation
↓
validate
↓
sync
↓
atomic root switch
```

---

# 241. Versioned Backups

Backups should include:

```text
application_id
build_id
schema_id
storage_format
generation
timestamp
```

Timestamp is metadata, not part of canonical content hashing.

---

# 242. Reproducibility

For deterministic snapshots:

```text
ordering
encoding
schema
```

must be deterministic.

Volatile metadata should be excluded from content hash.

---

# 243. Content Hash

A snapshot content hash covers:

```text
canonical schema
+
canonical records
```

not machine-specific paths.

---

# 244. AI Tooling

Axiom compiler artifacts should expose:

```text
type schema
field semantics
serialization format
migration graph
storage layout
index definitions
```

in machine-readable metadata.

This supports AI-assisted code generation and maintenance.

---

# 245. AI Safety

AI tooling must not infer that:

```text
field id 3
```

can be reused merely because the field is no longer referenced in current source.

---

# 246. Schema Documentation

Generated schema documentation may contain:

```text
type
field
ID
required/optional
default
version
compatibility
secret status
```

# 247. Compiler Command

outputs schema metadata without executing application code.

Required components:

# 252. Round-Trip Property

For supported values:

```text
decode(encode(x)) == x
```

under semantic equality.

---

# 253. Canonical Property

For canonical values:

```text
encode(decode(bytes)) == canonical(bytes)
```

where the input is valid canonical data.

---

# 254. Schema Evolution Property

For every declared compatible schema transition:

```text
decode_new(encode_old(value))
```

must produce the documented result.

---

# 255. WAL Property

After simulated crash:

```text
recover(store)
```

must result in:

```text
committed transactions preserved

```

within the documented model.

---

# 256. Index Property

After recovery:

```text
index(key) == primary_store(key)
```

for every committed record.

---

# 257. Snapshot Property

A reader observing generation `G` must see a consistent view of generation `G`.

---

# 258. Concurrency Property

Multiple readers must not corrupt:

```text
page cache
schema cache
index
WAL
```

---

# 259. Resource Property

No malformed input may bypass:

```text
decode limits
storage quotas
transaction limits
page limits
```

---

# 260. Security Property

No serialized input may cause:

```text
arbitrary code execution
```

merely by decoding.

---

# 261. No Deserialization Constructors

Decoding must not invoke arbitrary user constructors automatically.

Generated decode functions create validated values directly.

---

# 262. Validation Hooks

Applications may request:

```axiom
decode_validated<T>()
```

which runs explicit validation after structural decoding.

---

# 263. Validation Separation

Structural validity:

```text
correct binary representation
```

is separate from domain validity:

```text
age <= 150
email valid
balance >= 0
```

---

# 264. Domain Validation

Domain validation remains ordinary Axiom code.

This avoids embedding business rules in the serializer.

---

# 265. Serialization Security Boundary

Untrusted input should follow:

```text
bytes
↓
bounded decoder
↓
structural validation
↓
domain validation
↓
application
```

---

# 266. Persistent Storage Security Boundary

```text
untrusted storage
↓
page validation
↓
checksum
↓
schema validation
↓
record validation
↓
application
```

---

# 267. Performance Target

The generated serializer should approach hand-written binary serialization.

Target overhead:

```text
primitive encode ≈ direct store
primitive decode ≈ direct load + bounds check
```

---

# 268. Allocation Target

Simple fixed-size structs:

```text
zero temporary heap allocations
```

Variable-length fields allocate only required memory.

---

# 269. Zero-Copy Target

For immutable input:

```text
view decode
```

should require:

```text
O(1)
```

additional allocation for fixed-layout data.

---

# 270. Persistent Store Performance

The page store should support:

- sequential append
- indexed lookup
- range scan
- concurrent readers
- one writer

without requiring heavyweight runtime machinery.

---

# 271. Binary Size

A program using only:

```text
struct serialization
```

should not link:

```text
WAL
BTree
KV
compaction
```

unless referenced.

---

# 272. ABI Stability

Serialized representation is independent from:

```text
Axiom compiler version
```

provided the schema remains compatible.

---

# 273. Compiler Version Independence

A newer compiler can read old AXBIN data when schema compatibility rules permit it.

---

# 274. Runtime Version Independence

AXBIN decoding should not require the exact same runtime version.

Only the stable format contract matters.

---

# 275. Format Registry

Reserved format identifiers:

```text
AXBIN
AXBF
AXSN
AXDB
```

must be centrally specified to avoid collisions.

---

# 276. Magic Numbers

Every persistent container has a recognizable magic value.

Invalid magic must fail before deeper parsing.

---

# 277. Version Negotiation

Unsupported format versions return:

```text
UnsupportedVersion
```

rather than guessing.

---

# 278. Forward Compatibility

Readers may skip unknown optional metadata.

They must reject unknown mandatory semantics.

---

# 279. Backward Compatibility

New writers may emit fields understood by older readers only when compatibility is explicitly guaranteed.

---

# 280. Schema Compatibility Matrix

Generated metadata should expose:

```text
V1 → V2 : compatible
V2 → V3 : migration required
V3 → V4 : breaking
```

This is metadata, not an automatic migration decision.

# 287. Batch API

```axiom

    batch.remove(...)
```

# 288. Atomic Batch

The batch is atomic within one storage instance.

It is not automatically atomic across:

```text
multiple stores
filesystem + network
multiple processes
```

---

# 289. Cross-Store Transactions

Not part of 612.

A higher distributed/application transaction layer may coordinate them.

---

# 290. Transaction Hooks

Optional hooks:

```text
before_commit
after_commit
after_abort
```

must not execute arbitrary external side effects as though those effects were transactional.

---

# 291. External Side Effects

A transaction commit cannot atomically include:

```text
email
network request
GPU operation
external process
```

without a higher-level protocol.

---

# 292. Outbox Pattern

612 primitives can implement:

```text
database transaction
+
persistent outbox
```

for reliable external event delivery.

---

# 293. Event Outbox

Example:

```text
update state
+
append event
→
commit
```

A separate dispatcher sends the event later.

---

# 294. Inbox Pattern

A persistent inbox can record processed message IDs.

This helps build idempotent IPC/network services.

---

# 295. Idempotency Key

A persistent store may use:

```text
RequestId → Result
```

to detect duplicate requests.

---

# 296. Service Recovery

BOOTSTRAP-605 can restore service state from:

```text
snapshot
+
WAL
+
inbox/outbox
```

---

# 297. Checkpoint Integration

The service supervisor should know:

```text
storage generation
```

when recording a service checkpoint.

---

# 298. Diagnostics Integration

Storage events include:

```text
transaction_id
generation
schema_id
page_id
```

where useful.

---

# 299. Trace Correlation

Storage spans inherit the current:

```text
task_id
service_id
trace_id
transaction_id
```

---

# 300. Final Architecture

```text
                         AXIOM APPLICATION
                                │
                    ┌───────────▼───────────┐
                    │   Typed Domain Data   │
                    └───────────┬───────────┘
                                │
              ┌─────────────────▼─────────────────┐
              │       Serialization Layer         │
              │ AXBIN / Schema / Codec / Views    │
              └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                │
          ┌─────────────────────▼─────────────────────┐
          │       Structured Storage Layer             │
          │ KV / BTree / Persistent Collections       │
          │ WAL / Pages / Indexes / Snapshots         │
          └─────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                │
                     ┌──────────▼──────────┐
                     │ Storage Transactions│
                     └──────────┬──────────┘
                                │
                     BOOTSTRAP-611
                                │
                ┌───────────────▼───────────────┐
                │ File / mmap / VFS / Durability│
                └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                │
        ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
        │                       │                       │
       603                     606                     607
    Security                 Resources              Scheduler
        │                       │                       │
        └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┘
                                │
                     Native Operating System
```

---

# 301. Core Invariants

The implementation is correct only if:

```text
I1   Canonical encoding is deterministic.
I2   Portable encoding is architecture-independent.
I3   Malformed input cannot violate memory safety.
I4   Decode limits are enforced.
I5   Persistent field IDs are stable.
I6   Unknown optional fields can be skipped.
I7   Required fields are validated.
I8   Schema incompatibility is explicit.
I9   Migration is explicit.
I10  Serialization does not require runtime reflection.
I11  Simple serialization does not require heap allocation.
I12  Zero-copy views cannot outlive their source.
I13  Persistent data contains no native pointers.
I14  WAL precedes durable page mutation.
I15  Committed transactions survive documented crashes.
I16  Uncommitted transactions are not exposed as committed.
I17  Snapshot readers see a consistent generation.
I18  Indexes remain consistent with committed primary data.
I19  Storage quotas are enforced.
I20  Corrupt data cannot become arbitrary executable behavior.
I21  Secret fields are not leaked through diagnostics.
I22  Database functionality is dead-strippable.
I23  The serializer is independent of filesystem implementation.
I24  The storage engine is independent of language GC.
I25  Cross-process exactly-once semantics are not falsely claimed.
I26  External side effects are not implicitly transactional.
I27  Format versions are validated.
I28  Schema identity is independent of source formatting.
I29  Persistent object references are logical IDs/offsets, not pointers.
I30  Recovery is deterministic under the same storage state.
```

---

# 302. Acceptance Criteria

BOOTSTRAP-612 is complete when:

1. AXBIN primitive encoding is specified.
2. Fixed-width integers work.
3. Variable-width integers work.
4. Signed integers use canonical encoding.
5. Boolean encoding is canonical.
6. Floating-point encoding is deterministic.
7. NaN canonicalization works.
8. UTF-8 strings are supported.
9. Raw bytes are supported.
10. Arrays are supported.
11. Fixed arrays are supported.
12. Structs are supported.
13. Enums are supported.
14. Tagged unions are supported.
15. Options are supported.
16. Results are supported.
17. Maps are supported.
18. Sets are supported.
19. Canonical map ordering works.
20. Length bounds are enforced.
21. Decode depth limits work.
22. Allocation limits work.
23. Schema IDs are deterministic.
24. Schema versions are represented.
25. Field IDs are stable.
26. Unknown optional fields are skippable.
27. Required fields are validated.
28. Compatible schema evolution is supported.
29. Breaking schema changes are detected.
30. Explicit migration works.
31. Compiler-generated serializers work.
32. Compiler-generated schemas work.
33. Reflection is not required.
34. Zero-copy views work.
35. View lifetime is safe.
36. Streaming encoding works.
37. Streaming decoding works.
38. AXBIN framing works.
39. Checksums work.
40. WAL works.
41. WAL recovery works.
42. Page checksums work.
43. Page corruption is detected.
44. Single-writer transactions work.
45. Snapshot readers work.
46. Persistent KV works.
47. Persistent vector works.
48. Persistent map works.
49. Persistent log works.
50. Ordered range scans work.
51. Indexes work.
52. Unique indexes work.
53. Snapshot creation works.
54. Snapshot restore works.
55. Crash recovery works.
56. Power-loss simulation works.
57. Storage quotas work.
58. Large blobs stream without full-memory allocation.
59. Compaction preserves correctness.
60. Dead stripping removes unused database components.
61. IPC can use AXBIN.
62. Networking can use AXBIN.
63. Application state can use AXBIN snapshots.
64. Config can use generated binary snapshots.
65. Encryption can wrap persistent storage.
66. Diagnostics contain storage correlation IDs.
67. Secret values remain redacted.
68. Fuzzing cannot violate memory safety.
69. Malformed input cannot cause unbounded resource consumption.
70. Generated serialization approaches hand-written binary-code performance.

---

# 303. Architectural Conclusion

BOOTSTRAP-612 deliberately establishes a **layered data foundation rather than prematurely creating a giant database subsystem**.

The fundamental progression is:

```text
Axiom Value
    ↓
Schema
    ↓
Canonical Binary Representation
    ↓
Serialized Bytes
    ↓
Storage Record
    ↓
Page
    ↓
WAL / Transaction
    ↓
Durable Storage
```

This allows Axiom to support all of the following without adding a mandatory database runtime:

```text
configuration snapshots
application state
IPC
network protocols
binary assets
persistent collections
embedded KV stores
event logs
caches
AI model metadata
indexes
embedded databases
```

The key architectural choice is:

> **Serialization is a compiler/data-model capability; persistence is a storage capability; database querying is a higher-level capability.**

That separation keeps the language fast, modular and dead-strippable while still allowing Axiom to build a full native database stack entirely in Axiom itself.

**BOOTSTRAP-612 COMPLETE.**

---

# 304. Next Architecture Task

## BOOTSTRAP-613 — Native Compression, Archive, Package, Content-Addressed Storage & Resource Packaging Runtime 5.0

The next layer will build on **611 Storage + 612 Serialization** and define:

- compression abstraction
- streaming compression/decompression
- archive format abstraction
- ZIP/TAR-like compatibility boundary
- native Axiom package format
- executable/resource bundles
- package manifests
- content-addressed objects
- deduplication
- chunking
- Merkle trees
- immutable resources
- package verification
- signed packages through 610
- encrypted packages
- compressed storage
- random-access compressed assets
- package mounting through VFS
- package versioning
- dependency/resource manifests
- offline package deployment
- deterministic package generation
- reproducible package hashes
- AI-readable package metadata
- asset indexing
- model/large-file packaging
- lazy resource loading
- memory mapping of package contents
- package cache
- content-addressed cache
- garbage collection of **storage objects**, explicitly separate from Axiom memory GC
- compiler/linker integration
- dead stripping
- native executable/resource bundling
- Windows/Linux/macOS/Android/iOS/WASM packaging boundaries.

**BOOTSTRAP-612 COMPLETE → BOOTSTRAP-613 QUEUED.**

:::writing{variant="document" id="73146" title="BOOTSTRAP-613 — Native Compression, Archive, Package, Content-Addressed Storage & Resource Packaging Runtime 5.0"}

# BOOTSTRAP-613 — Native Compression, Archive, Package, Content-Addressed Storage & Resource Packaging Runtime 5.0

**Status:** Architecture Specification — Completed  
**Layer:** Native Runtime / Storage / Packaging  
**Depends on:** BOOTSTRAP-600..612  
**Primary dependencies:** 603 Security, 606 Resource Governor, 610 Cryptography, 611 Storage/VFS, 612 Serialization  
**Design priority:** native performance, deterministic output, minimal runtime dependency, secure-by-default, AI-readable metadata.

---

## 1. Purpose

BOOTSTRAP-613 defines Axiom's native runtime and toolchain architecture for:

- compression/decompression;
- archive reading/writing;
- native package format;
- application/resource bundles;
- content-addressed storage;
- deduplication;
- chunking;
- Merkle trees;
- immutable objects;
- package signing and verification;
- optional encryption;
- package mounting through VFS;
- package cache;
- offline deployment;
- package updates and rollback;
- resource indexing and lazy loading;
- deterministic and reproducible package generation.

The subsystem must work both as:

1. a **runtime library** for applications;
2. a **compiler/linker resource-packaging layer**;
3. a **deployment/package toolchain**;
4. a **VFS backend**;
5. a **content-addressed local object store**.

---

# 2. Core Design Principles

### P613-01 — Packages are data, not code

Opening, inspecting, mounting, decompressing or validating a package must never execute package-provided code.

### P613-02 — Verification precedes trust

A package may be:

```text
readable
→ structurally valid
→ integrity verified
→ cryptographically authenticated
→ policy authorized
→ activated
```

These are distinct states.

### P613-03 — Immutable package contents

Once an object or activated package generation is committed, its contents are immutable.

Updates create new objects/generations.

### P613-04 — Content addressing

Objects are identified by cryptographic digest rather than mutable filenames.

```text
ObjectId = Hash(algorithm || domain || canonical_content)
```

### P613-05 — Deterministic builds

Given identical logical inputs and build parameters, package generation must produce identical canonical metadata and, where codec determinism is supported, identical package bytes.

### P613-06 — Streaming first

Large resources must not require loading the complete resource into RAM.

### P613-07 — VFS integration

A package can be mounted as a read-only filesystem layer without extracting every entry.

### P613-08 — No mandatory external runtime

The core package runtime must not depend on a third-party package manager, compression framework or runtime.

Optional codec/provider modules may exist behind explicit interfaces.

---

# 3. Layer Architecture

```text
Application
    │
    ▼
Resource API
    │
    ├── Package API
    ├── Archive API
    └── Content Store API
            │
            ▼
       Package Engine
            │
     ┌──────┼─────────┐
     ▼      ▼         ▼
Compression Integrity Encryption
     │      │         │
     └──────┼─────────┘
            ▼
       VFS / Storage
            │
            ▼
BOOTSTRAP-611 Storage
            │
            ▼
Native OS / Device
```

---

# 4. Terminology

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Package | Immutable logical collection of resources |
| Entry | One named resource inside a package |
| Object | Immutable content-addressed byte sequence |
| Chunk | Independently addressable object fragment |
| Manifest | Canonical package metadata |
| Package ID | Stable logical identity |
| Generation | Immutable activated version |
| Object ID | Cryptographic identity of content |
| Merkle Root | Cryptographic root representing a tree |
| Store | Local content-addressed object repository |
| Mount | Exposing package contents through VFS |
| Pin | Prevents object reclamation |
| Lease | Temporary retention guarantee |
| Bundle | Package containing executable + resources |
| Resource | Application-consumable package entry |

---

# 5. Compression Architecture

Compression is exposed through a common interface:

```text
CompressionCodec
    name()
    version()
    capabilities()
    create_encoder(config)
    create_decoder(config)
```

A codec must declare:

```text
streaming
dictionary
random_access
deterministic
checksum
parallel
native
```

capabilities.

---

# 6. Built-In Compression Modes

The core format defines these logical modes:

```text
STORE
DEFLATE
LZ4
ZSTD
BROTLI
CUSTOM
```

`STORE` is mandatory.

Other codecs may be compiled into profiles or supplied as optional providers.

The package format stores the codec identifier, so decoding does not depend on filename extensions.

---

# 7. Compression Levels

Compression configuration:

```text
CompressionConfig {
    codec
    level
    block_size
    window_size
    dictionary_id
    deterministic
}
```

Levels are codec-specific.

The package metadata records the actual codec and parameters required for decoding.

A codec must reject unsupported parameter combinations rather than silently changing them.

---

# 8. Deterministic Compression

Deterministic mode must eliminate:

- random seeds;
- wall-clock timestamps;
- nondeterministic block ordering;
- process-dependent metadata;
- host-specific information.

The package builder must therefore control:

```text
input ordering
metadata ordering
timestamps
compression parameters
dictionary
codec version
```

Codec versions that cannot guarantee deterministic output must not be used for reproducible builds.

---

# 9. Streaming Compression

API:

```text
Compressor
    write(bytes)
    flush(mode)
    finish()

Decompressor
    read()
    feed(bytes)
    finish()
```

Streaming operation must support:

```text
small resource
large file
network stream
pipe
memory mapped input
VFS input
```

No complete-resource allocation is required.

---

# 10. Compression Blocks

Large entries may be split into independent compressed blocks.

```text
Entry
 ├── Block 0
 ├── Block 1
 ├── Block 2
 └── ...
```

Each block contains:

```text
uncompressed_size
compressed_size
codec
checksum
object_id
```

This enables:

- partial reads;
- parallel decompression;
- random access;
- corruption localization;
- content deduplication.

---

# 11. Random-Access Compression

For resources requiring random access:

```text
compressed entry
        │
        ├── block index
        ├── compressed block 0
        ├── compressed block 1
        └── ...
```

The index maps:

```text
logical_offset → block_id
```

Reading a range therefore requires only the necessary blocks.

Target:

```text
O(log N)
```

index lookup plus decompression of required blocks.

---

# 12. Compression Heuristics

Package builder may select:

```text
STORE
```

when:

```text
compressed_size >= original_size
```

unless deterministic package policy explicitly requires the codec.

For already-compressed data:

```text
jpg
png
mp4
zip
gzip
7z
encrypted data
```

the default policy should prefer `STORE`.

---

# 13. Checksums

Every independently stored compressed block must support integrity verification.

Minimum:

```text
CRC32C
```

for corruption detection.

Cryptographic integrity:

```text
SHA-256
SHA-512/256
```

or another algorithm approved by BOOTSTRAP-610.

Checksum and cryptographic hash have different purposes.

---

# 14. Archive Abstraction

Archive API:

```text
ArchiveReader
    open()
    entry_count()
    find(path)
    open_entry(path)
    iterate()

ArchiveWriter
    add(path, source)
    remove(path)
    finalize()
```

Archive readers must be able to inspect metadata without extracting contents.

---

# 15. Compatibility Formats

Axiom supports import/export boundaries for:

```text
ZIP
TAR
TAR.GZ
TAR.ZSTD
```

Compatibility is not the native package format.

The native package format is optimized for:

- deterministic builds;
- random access;
- signatures;
- content addressing;
- VFS mounting;
- deduplication;
- immutable storage.

---

# 16. Native Package Format

Canonical extension:

```text
.axpk
```

Logical structure:

```text
AXPK
├── Header
├── Manifest
├── Entry Index
├── Object Index
├── Chunk/Merkle Index
├── Payload Objects
└── Signature Area
```

---

# 17. AXPK Header

Conceptual header:

```text
AxpkHeader {
    magic
    format_version
    flags
    header_size
    manifest_offset
    manifest_size
    index_offset
    index_size
    object_table_offset
    object_table_size
    signature_offset
    signature_size
    package_id
    generation
    manifest_hash
}
```

All integer fields use explicit endianness.

Canonical format:

```text
little-endian
```

unless a future format version explicitly changes this.

---

# 18. Package Identity

```text
PackageId
```

is a stable logical identifier.

Example:

```text
com.example.myapp
```

Version:

```text
major.minor.patch
```

Generation is separate from semantic version.

Example:

```text
Package:
    com.example.myapp
    version = 2.4.1
    generation = 17
```

---

# 19. Target Constraints

Package metadata may specify:

```text
os
architecture
abi
minimum_os
cpu_features
gpu_features
runtime_profile
```

Example:

```text
targets:
    windows-x64
    linux-x64
    macos-arm64
```

Target-specific resources can coexist inside one logical package.

---

# 20. Package Manifest

Manifest uses AXBIN/AXBF from BOOTSTRAP-612.

Example:

```text
PackageManifest {
    package_id
    version
    generation
    format_version
    targets[]
    entries[]
    dependencies[]
    capabilities[]
    publisher
    signatures[]
    compression_policy
    encryption_policy
    resource_groups[]
}
```

The manifest is canonicalized before hashing.

---

# 21. Entry Model

```text
PackageEntry {
    path
    kind
    size
    content_id
    codec
    flags
    mode
    attributes
    mime_type?
    locale?
    variant?
}
```

Entry kinds:

```text
File
Directory
Symlink
Executable
SharedLibrary
Resource
Manifest
Index
```

Symlink support is policy-controlled.

---

# 22. Package Paths

Package paths must:

- use UTF-8;
- use `/`;
- never contain `..`;
- never begin with `/`;
- never contain NUL;
- have normalized separators;
- use canonical Unicode normalization according to package policy.

Examples:

```text
assets/logo.png
models/main.axmodel
locales/vi/app.axres
bin/app.exe
```

---

# 23. Path Traversal Prevention

The package engine must reject:

```text
../secret
../../file
/absolute/path
C:\Windows\...
\\server\...
```

when interpreted as package-relative paths.

Extraction must occur through BOOTSTRAP-611 secure path APIs rather than raw concatenation.

---

# 24. Symlink Policy

Default:

```text
symlink = disabled
```

If enabled:

- target must be validated;
- package-relative targets cannot escape package root;
- host-absolute targets require explicit privileged policy.

Packages must never silently create arbitrary host filesystem links.

---

# 25. Object Model

Content-addressed objects:

```text
ObjectId
ObjectHeader
Payload
```

Conceptually:

```text
ObjectId = H(domain || type || size || payload)
```

The domain separator prevents cross-type hash ambiguity.

---

# 26. Object Types

```text
RawBlob
CompressedBlock
Manifest
EntryIndex
ChunkIndex
MerkleNode
Package
Delta
Dictionary
Metadata
```

---

# 27. Immutable Object Store

Logical API:

```text
ObjectStore
    put(source) -> ObjectId
    open(id)
    exists(id)
    stat(id)
    pin(id)
    unpin(id)
    lease(id, duration)
    delete(id)
    collect()
```

`put()` must be idempotent.

If the same object already exists:

```text
put(content) → existing ObjectId
```

without creating duplicate physical data.

---

# 28. Object Storage Layout

Implementation may use:

```text
objects/
    ab/
       cdef...
```

where the first digest bytes determine directories.

The exact layout is implementation-defined.

Applications must never depend on physical object paths.

---

# 29. Chunking

Large files may use fixed or content-defined chunks.

Modes:

```text
FixedChunk
ContentDefinedChunk
```

Default target chunk size:

```text
256 KiB – 4 MiB
```

depending on workload.

Chunk size is a package policy, not a language semantic.

---

# 30. Content-Defined Chunking

CDC may use rolling fingerprints.

Boundary selection:

```text
rolling_hash(data)
        ↓
boundary decision
        ↓
chunk
```

Advantages:

- stable chunks after insertion/deletion;
- better incremental updates;
- deduplication across package versions.

CDC parameters must be recorded in package metadata.

---

# 31. Merkle Tree

A package can be represented as:

```text
             Root
            /    \
         Node    Node
        /   \    /   \
      Obj   Obj Obj   Obj
```

Each node contains hashes of children.

The root provides a compact identity for the complete logical content tree.

---

# 32. Merkle Domains

Different node types use domain separation:

```text
AXPK-MANIFEST
AXPK-ENTRY
AXPK-CHUNK
AXPK-MERKLE
AXPK-PACKAGE
```

This prevents structural hash collisions between semantic object classes.

---

# 33. Deduplication

Deduplication occurs at:

```text
whole-object
chunk
package
resource
```

levels.

Deduplication must not alter logical package semantics.

---

# 34. Deduplication Across Packages

Example:

```text
Package A
    model.bin
        chunk A
        chunk B
        chunk C

Package B
    model.bin
        chunk A
        chunk B
        chunk D
```

Only:

```text
A
B
C
D
```

are stored once.

---

# 35. Storage Garbage Collection

Storage-object reclamation is distinct from language memory management.

It operates on:

```text
roots
→ reachable objects
→ unreachable objects
```

It must never be described as Axiom heap GC.

---

# 36. Storage GC Roots

Roots include:

```text
active package generations
installed packages
explicit pins
leases
snapshots
deployment generations
cache entries
application state references
```

---

# 37. Reclamation Algorithm

Default:

```text
mark reachable
→ identify unreachable
→ reclaim
```

Alternative:

```text
reference counting
```

may be used as an optimization.

Reference counting alone must not be assumed sufficient when cycles exist.

---

# 38. Pins

A pin prevents reclamation.

```text
pin(ObjectId)
```

is intended for:

- active deployment;
- memory-mapped resource;
- ongoing update;
- long-running process;
- package mount.

Pins must be released deterministically.

---

# 39. Leases

A lease is time-bounded:

```text
Lease {
    object_id
    expiration
}
```

Expired leases become reclaimable.

Clock handling must use BOOTSTRAP-601/607 time abstractions.

---

# 40. Package Cache

Caches are separate from authoritative package state.

Namespaces:

```text
SystemCache
UserCache
ApplicationCache
BuildCache
CompilerCache
ModelCache
```

Each cache has:

```text
quota
eviction policy
integrity policy
encryption policy
```

---

# 41. Cache Eviction

Eviction may use:

```text
LRU
LFU
size-aware LRU
age + size
custom policy
```

Eviction must never remove:

```text
active generation
pinned object
leased object
required dependency
```

---

# 42. Package Mount

A package can be exposed as:

```text
/vfs/app
```

through BOOTSTRAP-611.

Mount properties:

```text
read_only
package_id
generation
trust_state
capability
```

---

# 43. Package Filesystem

Example:

```text
app.axpk
    ↓
AXPK filesystem
    ↓
VFS
    ↓
Application
```

No extraction is necessary for ordinary reads.

---

# 44. Overlay Packages

Multiple package layers can be combined:

```text
Base Package
    ↓
Patch Package
    ↓
Localization Package
    ↓
User Override
```

Lookup order must be explicit and deterministic.

Example:

```text
override
→ localization
→ patch
→ base
```

---

# 45. Package Overlay Security

An overlay must not silently replace:

```text
executable
shared library
security policy
manifest
```

unless the deployment policy explicitly permits replacement.

Resource-only overlays can be given narrower capabilities.

---

# 46. Executable Bundles

Axiom supports logical executable bundles:

```text
Application Bundle
├── executable
├── libraries
├── resources
├── models
├── locales
├── configuration defaults
└── metadata
```

The actual native platform packaging remains a separate layer.

---

# 47. Native Platform Mapping

### Windows

```text
EXE
DLL
resources
AXPK
```

can be assembled into deployment artifacts.

### Linux

```text
ELF
.so
resources
AXPK
```

### macOS

```text
.app
├── Contents/MacOS
├── Contents/Resources
└── Contents/Frameworks
```

### iOS

Resources must obey Apple application-bundle and signing restrictions.

### Android

Axiom packages are internal deployment resources; final APK/AAB integration is handled by the platform packager.

### WASM

Resources are exposed through:

```text
embedded data
host-provided VFS
package blob
```

according to the host environment.

---

# 48. Resource Compiler

Compiler/linker can transform:

```text
image
audio
shader
font
model
translation
binary data
```

into package entries.

Example:

```text
@resource("assets/logo.png")
const logo = resource(...)
```

The compiler generates resource metadata rather than copying arbitrary data into source code.

---

# 49. Embedded Resources

Small resources may be embedded directly in native binaries.

Policy:

```text
embed_if_size <= threshold
```

Large resources remain external/package-backed.

This avoids unnecessarily increasing executable memory footprint.

---

# 50. Resource Selection

Resources may contain:

```text
locale
region
theme
resolution
architecture
platform
feature_set
```

Example:

```text
icons/logo@windows.png
icons/logo@linux.png
icons/logo@android.png
```

Selection occurs through a deterministic resolver.

---

# 51. Localization

Package resource variants:

```text
locale = vi-VN
locale = en-US
locale = ja-JP
```

Fallback:

```text
vi-VN
→ vi
→ default
```

Fallback order must be deterministic.

---

# 52. Lazy Resource Loading

Resource API:

```text
ResourceHandle<T>
    metadata()
    open()
    read()
    map()
    preload()
```

Resources are loaded only when requested unless marked:

```text
eager
```

---

# 53. Memory Mapping

Uncompressed, aligned entries may be memory mapped directly.

Requirements:

```text
stored
uncompressed
page-aligned
immutable
```

Compressed entries cannot generally be directly memory mapped.

They require:

```text
decompression
```

or block-level cached views.

---

# 54. Resource Views

Large resources can expose:

```text
ByteView
TypedView<T>
Stream
BlockReader
```

without copying the entire resource.

Typed views must validate:

```text
alignment
size
endianness
format version
```

before access.

---

# 55. Model Packaging

Large AI/model resources can be represented as:

```text
model manifest
weights
tokenizer
configuration
metadata
optional quantization tables
```

Individual tensors/files may be separately chunked.

This permits partial loading.

---

# 56. Large-File Streaming

The runtime must support:

```text
open
seek
read_range
stream
prefetch
cancel
```

for multi-gigabyte assets without full materialization.

---

# 57. Prefetch

Resource prefetch may be:

```text
explicit
heuristic
package-declared
```

Example:

```text
resource.prefetch(range)
```

Prefetch is advisory and must respect BOOTSTRAP-606 budgets.

---

# 58. Dependency Manifest

Package dependencies:

```text
Dependency {
    package_id
    version_constraint
    optional
    target_constraint
    feature_constraint
}
```

The runtime validates dependencies but does not have to implement a complete public package registry.

Dependency resolution belongs to a higher deployment layer.

---

# 59. Dependency Integrity

Resolved dependencies must identify:

```text
PackageId
Version
Generation
ManifestHash
MerkleRoot
PublisherKeyId
```

A package must not silently substitute an unrelated dependency with the same name.

---

# 60. Offline Deployment

A complete offline deployment may contain:

```text
package
dependencies
object store
trust roots
deployment manifest
```

Installation must require no network connection.

---

# 61. Package Installation

Installation is transactional:

```text
stage
→ validate
→ verify
→ materialize objects
→ resolve dependencies
→ prepare generation
→ commit
→ activate
```

Failure before commit must leave the previous active generation unchanged.

---

# 62. Atomic Activation

Deployment state:

```text
generation 16 → active
generation 17 → staged
```

After successful commit:

```text
generation 17 → active
generation 16 → rollback candidate
```

The activation record itself must be updated atomically using BOOTSTRAP-611 durability primitives.

---

# 63. Rollback

Rollback switches the active generation pointer.

It does not modify immutable package contents.

Example:

```text
active = generation 17

failure

active = generation 16
```

---

# 64. Crash Recovery

If installation crashes:

```text
staging generation
```

remains incomplete.

On restart:

```text
detect incomplete transaction
→ validate journal
→ discard or resume
→ preserve active generation
```

No partially installed package may become active.

---

# 65. Package Uninstall

Uninstall removes logical references.

It does not immediately delete shared objects.

Later storage GC determines whether objects remain reachable.

This prevents one package uninstall from corrupting another package.

---

# 66. Package Updates

Update may reuse:

```text
unchanged objects
unchanged chunks
unchanged resources
```

Only new objects are transferred/stored.

---

# 67. Delta Packages

Optional delta package:

```text
BaseRoot
TargetRoot
AddedObjects[]
RemovedObjects[]
Metadata
```

The target package must be reconstructed and independently verified.

A delta must never be trusted merely because the base package was trusted.

---

# 68. Binary Delta Boundary

Binary delta algorithms are optional.

They must operate below the logical package API:

```text
Package
    ↓
Object/chunk graph
    ↓
Delta
```

The package semantics remain unchanged.

---

# 69. Package Encryption

Package contents may be encrypted using BOOTSTRAP-610.

Two modes:

```text
whole-package encryption
per-entry encryption
```

Per-entry encryption is preferred for random-access resources.

---

# 70. Encryption Metadata

Encrypted entry metadata includes:

```text
algorithm
key_id
nonce/IV
authentication_tag
key_usage
```

Keys are references to BOOTSTRAP-610 key providers, not plaintext package metadata.

---

# 71. Encryption and Deduplication

Encrypted objects generally cannot be deduplicated across different keys/nonces.

Therefore:

```text
plaintext content address
```

and:

```text
ciphertext storage identity
```

must be treated as separate concepts.

No plaintext hash may be exposed where policy forbids information leakage.

---

# 72. Package Signatures

Package signatures cover a canonical representation containing:

```text
manifest hash
entry index hash
object/Merkle root
format version
package identity
target
```

Signature implementation is delegated to BOOTSTRAP-610.

---

# 73. Signature Verification

Verification states:

```text
Unsigned
Malformed
IntegrityValid
SignatureValid
TrustedPublisher
PolicyAuthorized
```

These states must not be collapsed.

---

# 74. Publisher Identity

Publisher metadata:

```text
publisher_id
key_id
algorithm
certificate/reference
```

Trust roots come from deployment policy.

Package metadata alone cannot establish trust.

---

# 75. Capability Declaration

Packages may declare required capabilities:

```text
filesystem.read
network.connect
gpu.compute
microphone
camera
process.spawn
```

These declarations integrate with BOOTSTRAP-603.

A package requesting a capability does not automatically receive it.

---

# 76. Package Security Boundary

Package processing must protect against:

- path traversal;
- malformed archives;
- decompression bombs;
- integer overflow;
- excessive entry count;
- excessive nesting;
- huge metadata;
- hash flooding;
- corrupted indexes;
- malicious symlinks;
- invalid Unicode;
- resource exhaustion.

---

# 77. Decompression Bomb Protection

Before extraction/decompression, enforce:

```text
max_compressed_size
max_uncompressed_size
max_ratio
max_entries
max_nested_archives
max_cpu_time
```

All limits come from BOOTSTRAP-606 policy where applicable.

---

# 78. Archive Nesting

Automatic recursive extraction is prohibited.

If an entry contains another archive:

```text
resource data
```

not an instruction to recursively unpack.

Explicit application code must request nested processing.

---

# 79. Package Open Is Non-Executable

The following operations must never execute package content:

```text
open
mount
index
hash
verify
inspect
extract
```

Executable loading requires a separate privileged loader operation.

---

# 80. Executable Loading Boundary

Execution requires:

```text
package trust
→ signature policy
→ platform loader validation
→ capability policy
→ executable permission
→ process creation
```

BOOTSTRAP-613 does not bypass OS executable signing policies.

---

# 81. Dynamic Libraries

Dynamic libraries inside packages are treated as executable objects.

Loading requires explicit policy.

Library search must not accidentally allow an untrusted package to shadow trusted system libraries.

---

# 82. Package Inspection CLI

Conceptual commands:

```text
axiom pkg info app.axpk
axiom pkg list app.axpk
axiom pkg verify app.axpk
axiom pkg tree app.axpk
axiom pkg hash app.axpk
axiom pkg extract app.axpk out/
axiom pkg mount app.axpk /mnt/app
```

---

# 83. Object Store CLI

```text
axiom store stat <object>
axiom store verify
axiom store gc
axiom store pin <object>
axiom store unpin <object>
axiom store list
axiom store vacuum
```

---

# 84. Deterministic Entry Ordering

Canonical package entry order:

```text
UTF-8 normalized path
```

lexicographically sorted by byte representation.

Directories must not be dependent on host filesystem enumeration order.

---

# 85. Timestamp Normalization

Reproducible builds default to:

```text
timestamp = omitted
```

or an explicitly supplied build epoch.

Host filesystem timestamps must never silently enter package identity.

---

# 86. Permission Normalization

Portable packages must not embed arbitrary host-specific permissions.

Platform-specific permissions require explicit target metadata.

---

# 87. Host Metadata Exclusion

By default exclude:

```text
absolute source paths
username
machine name
host timestamps
inode numbers
device IDs
filesystem-specific IDs
```

unless explicitly declared as package metadata.

---

# 88. Package Reproducibility

Reproducibility requires identical:

```text
source resources
manifest
metadata
codec versions
codec parameters
object chunking
ordering
build epoch
signing inputs
```

Signatures are treated separately because key material naturally differs between signing operations unless deterministic signing is supported.

---

# 89. Package Format Versioning

Header contains:

```text
format_major
format_minor
```

Rules:

```text
same major → compatible according to declared capabilities
different major → parser must reject unless compatibility adapter exists
```

---

# 90. Forward Compatibility

Unknown manifest fields may be ignored only when marked:

```text
optional
```

Unknown mandatory fields cause rejection.

Unknown entry types must not be interpreted heuristically.

---

# 91. Backward Compatibility

New runtime versions must retain readers for supported older package versions according to the declared compatibility window.

Writers should emit the oldest format that supports required features.

---

# 92. Package Index

Index maps:

```text
path → EntryId
EntryId → ObjectId[]
ObjectId → physical storage
```

Indexes may be memory mapped for large packages.

---

# 93. Index Integrity

Index data is independently validated against:

```text
manifest hash
object IDs
sizes
Merkle root
```

No index entry may cause the reader to access bytes outside the package boundaries.

---

# 94. Corruption Detection

Corruption may occur at:

```text
header
manifest
index
compressed block
object
Merkle node
signature
```

The runtime must identify the smallest known corrupt unit.

Example:

```text
Resource: model.bin
Chunk: 182
ObjectId: ...
Checksum: mismatch
```

---

# 95. Recovery

If an object is corrupted but can be reconstructed from:

```text
another package
cache
remote store
backup
```

the object may be repaired.

The repair process must verify the reconstructed ObjectId before replacing the missing/corrupt object.

---

# 96. Package Cache Repair

Caches are disposable.

If validation fails:

```text
mark invalid
delete/rebuild
```

rather than propagating corrupted cache data into authoritative package state.

---

# 97. Resource Store Quotas

BOOTP-606 integration:

```text
max_package_count
max_package_size
max_object_count
max_store_size
max_cache_size
max_uncompressed_read
max_decompression_cpu
```

---

# 98. Package I/O Scheduling

Large package operations must be submitted through BOOTSTRAP-607.

Examples:

```text
async read object
async decompress
async verify
async install
```

CPU-heavy compression/decompression uses appropriate executor classes.

---

# 99. Cancellation

Long operations support:

```text
CancelToken
Deadline
```

including:

```text
package verify
package install
compression
decompression
GC
index building
```

Cancellation must leave persistent state valid.

---

# 100. Synchronization

Concurrent package access uses BOOTSTRAP-608.

Requirements:

- multiple readers;
- controlled writer;
- atomic generation switch;
- no partially visible index;
- no deletion of pinned/active objects.

---

# 101. Storage Integration

BOOTSTRAP-611 provides:

```text
file
directory
atomic rename
fsync
mapping
locking
VFS
```

BOOTSTRAP-613 adds package semantics above them.

---

# 102. Serialization Integration

BOOTSTRAP-612 provides canonical encoding for:

```text
manifest
entry metadata
dependency metadata
resource metadata
object indexes
```

No second incompatible metadata serialization format should be introduced.

---

# 103. Cryptography Integration

BOOTSTRAP-610 provides:

```text
hash
MAC
AEAD
signatures
key storage
certificate/trust
secure random
```

BOOTSTRAP-613 only defines package-level composition.

---

# 104. Security Integration

BOOTSTRAP-603 controls:

```text
package mount
package extraction
package installation
executable loading
network package retrieval
store access
resource capabilities
```

---

# 105. Diagnostics Integration

BOOTSTRAP-602 events:

```text
PackageOpened
PackageVerified
PackageRejected
ObjectMissing
ObjectCorrupt
PackageMounted
PackageInstalled
PackageActivated
PackageRolledBack
StoreGCStarted
StoreGCCompleted
```

Sensitive metadata must be redacted.

---

# 106. State Integration

BOOTSTRAP-600 can persist:

```text
active package generation
installation transaction
rollback generation
store roots
resource cache state
```

Checkpointing must not capture transient decompression buffers as persistent state.

---

# 107. Configuration Integration

BOOTSTRAP-601 controls:

```text
cache locations
quotas
compression defaults
package trust roots
allowed codecs
maximum extraction size
store GC policy
package mount policy
```

Configuration changes are applied through immutable snapshots.

---

# 108. Supervision Integration

BOOTSTRAP-605 may supervise:

```text
package service
resource service
store maintenance worker
background GC
package updater
```

A package failure must not automatically imply application failure unless the service dependency graph says so.

---

# 109. Resource Governor Integration

BOOTSTRAP-606 accounts:

```text
storage bytes
compressed bytes
decompressed bytes
CPU time
I/O bandwidth
I/O operations
mapped bytes
cache bytes
object count
```

---

# 110. Compiler Integration

Compiler understands:

```text
@resource
@bundle
@package
@embed
@compress
@package_entry
```

Example:

```text
@resource("assets/logo.png")
const Logo = Resource<Bytes>;
```

Compiler emits package metadata rather than application-specific extraction code.

---

# 111. Linker Integration

Linker can:

```text
collect resources
merge resource sections
deduplicate identical objects
strip unused embedded resources
construct bundle manifest
```

Dead resources should be eliminated when static reachability proves they are unused and policy allows elimination.

---

# 112. Dead Stripping

Package-aware dead stripping operates on:

```text
code symbols
resource references
package entries
dependency graph
```

It must not remove entries explicitly marked:

```text
@public_resource
@runtime_discovered
```

---

# 113. Runtime-Discovered Resources

Applications may access dynamic paths:

```text
resources.open("plugins/" + name)
```

The compiler cannot always prove reachability.

Such resources require explicit manifest declarations.

---

# 114. AI-Readable Package Metadata

Every package should optionally contain:

```text
package.axmeta
```

containing machine-readable:

```text
package identity
schema
resources
dependencies
targets
capabilities
compression
encryption
signatures
content graph
```

The metadata must be deterministic and easy for tools/agents to inspect.

---

# 115. Package Graph

AI/tooling can inspect:

```text
Package
 ├── Dependency
 ├── Resource
 │    └── Object
 │         └── Chunk
 ├── Capability
 └── Target
```

This allows agents to understand package composition without scanning binary payloads.

---

# 116. Package Search Index

Optional index:

```text
resource name
type
locale
tags
size
hash
package
dependency
```

The index must remain derived data.

It can always be regenerated from canonical package metadata.

---

# 117. Content Addressability and Build Cache

Compiler outputs can be stored as objects:

```text
source hash
+ compiler version
+ target
+ flags
+ dependency hashes
        ↓
Artifact ObjectId
```

This integrates BOOTSTRAP-613 with Axiom's precompiled/cache requirement.

---

# 118. Compiler Artifact Cache

Example:

```text
source.ax
    ↓
canonical source identity
    ↓
semantic fingerprint
    ↓
IR fingerprint
    ↓
machine-code artifact
    ↓
ObjectStore
```

If all relevant inputs match, the compiler may reuse the artifact.

---

# 119. Cache Correctness

Cache identity must include all semantically relevant inputs:

```text
compiler version
target
ABI
CPU features
optimization level
language version
feature flags
dependencies
security policy
relevant source
```

Never reuse solely by source filename.

---

# 120. Package Build Pipeline

Canonical pipeline:

```text
collect inputs
    ↓
normalize
    ↓
hash
    ↓
chunk
    ↓
deduplicate
    ↓
compress
    ↓
build manifest
    ↓
build indexes
    ↓
build Merkle tree
    ↓
sign
    ↓
write AXPK
    ↓
verify
```

---

# 121. Build Verification

A package builder should automatically reopen its output and verify:

```text
header
manifest
indexes
objects
compression
hashes
Merkle root
signature
```

before declaring success.

---

# 122. Package Self-Check

CLI:

```text
axiom pkg verify --deep package.axpk
```

Modes:

```text
structural
integrity
deep
signature
runtime
```

---

# 123. Structural Verification

Checks:

- bounds;
- integer overflow;
- offsets;
- sizes;
- entry names;
- index consistency;
- version support.

No payload decompression is required.

---

# 124. Deep Verification

Deep verification additionally:

```text
decompress every block
verify every checksum
verify every ObjectId
verify Merkle root
```

This is expensive and therefore optional.

---

# 125. Package Mount Verification

Mount may use:

```text
lazy verification
```

for trusted local packages.

Security-sensitive deployments may require:

```text
full verification before mount
```

Policy determines behavior.

---

# 126. Trust Policy

Example:

```text
Development:
    unsigned allowed

Testing:
    signed preferred

Production:
    signed required

HighSecurity:
    signed + trusted publisher + encrypted
```

Policy is supplied by BOOTSTRAP-603/610.

---

# 127. Secure Temporary Files

Extraction and package staging must use BOOTSTRAP-611 secure temporary storage.

Requirements:

- unpredictable temporary identity;
- exclusive creation;
- restrictive permissions;
- cleanup on failure;
- no attacker-controlled filename reuse.

---

# 128. Atomic Package Writer

Package generation should write:

```text
temporary file
→ fsync
→ rename
→ fsync parent where required
```

rather than overwriting the target package directly.

---

# 129. Package Store Layout

Logical store:

```text
Store
├── objects
├── packages
├── generations
├── manifests
├── leases
├── pins
├── staging
└── indexes
```

Physical layout is implementation-defined.

---

# 130. Generation Registry

Registry:

```text
PackageId
    ├── version
    ├── generation
    ├── manifest_hash
    ├── merkle_root
    ├── active
    └── installation_state
```

The registry itself is transactional.

---

# 131. Multiple Generations

Old generations may remain for:

```text
rollback
diagnostics
shared dependencies
user selection
```

GC removes them only when unreachable.

---

# 132. Package Lifecycle

```text
Unknown
  ↓
Discovered
  ↓
Parsed
  ↓
Verified
  ↓
Staged
  ↓
Installed
  ↓
Activated
  ↓
Superseded
  ↓
Reclaimable
  ↓
Collected
```

---

# 133. Invalid Lifecycle

```text
Discovered
   ↓
Invalid
```

or:

```text
Installed
   ↓
Corrupt
   ↓
Quarantined
```

Corrupt packages must not automatically become active.

---

# 134. Quarantine

Security or integrity failures may move packages into:

```text
quarantine/
```

The package remains inspectable for diagnostics but is unavailable for execution/mount according to policy.

---

# 135. Package Removal

Removal sequence:

```text
disable activation
→ unmount
→ release pins
→ remove logical generation
→ update registry
→ background object GC
```

No immediate recursive physical deletion is required.

---

# 136. Mount Lifetime

A mounted package holds a reference/lease on:

```text
package generation
object index
required objects
```

This prevents concurrent storage GC from deleting active objects.

---

# 137. Multi-Process Access

Object stores may support concurrent processes through:

```text
atomic file operations
locks
generation records
append-only metadata
```

A process must not rely on process-local state for global correctness.

---

# 138. Store Locking

Lock granularity should favor:

```text
per-object
per-generation
per-registry
```

rather than one global lock.

Read operations should remain highly concurrent.

---

# 139. Crash-Safe Store GC

GC must tolerate process termination at any point.

A safe sequence:

```text
mark
→ persist mark generation
→ reclaim
→ commit
```

Interrupted GC must never delete an object that belongs to an active root.

---

# 140. Object Verification Before Reuse

Cached object:

```text
ObjectId X
```

may be reused only after:

```text
physical bytes
→ integrity verification
→ identity hash
→ X
```

This prevents corrupted cache poisoning.

---

# 141. Resource Limits

Package parser limits include:

```text
max_header
max_manifest
max_entries
max_path_length
max_dependency_count
max_chunk_count
max_object_size
max_total_size
max_nesting
```

All limits are explicit configuration.

---

# 142. Integer Safety

All size/offset calculations must use checked arithmetic.

Overflow:

```text
error
```

never wraparound.

---

# 143. Memory Safety

The package subsystem must avoid raw pointer arithmetic at the language API level.

Internal native implementation may use low-level operations only behind validated boundaries.

---

```text
resource_hash
```

may become constants.

```text
resource A
```

```text
ObjectId(A) == ObjectId(B)
```

```text
PackageNone
```

```text
ZIP

signatures
```

when not referenced.

# 156. Embedded Profile

Embedded targets may use:

```text
read-only AXPK

small index

no dynamic package updates
```

This keeps firmware small.

# 157. WASM Profile

```text
host-provided package

virtual filesystem
```

with all OS filesystem operations delegated to the host.

Android/iOS profiles must account for:

- read-only application resources;
- platform signing;
- storage lifecycle;
- background execution limits.
