```text
stable handles
versioned structs
function tables
schema IDs
```

Compiler-private runtime structures must not cross plugin boundaries.

---

# 144. FFI

Foreign activity providers can implement:

```text
ActivityProvider ABI
```

but FFI remains outside deterministic workflow code.

---

# 145. Crash Recovery Invariant

After process/node failure:

```text
durable workflow state
+
durable history
+
valid coordination ownership
```

must be sufficient to reconstruct the workflow.

---

# 146. No Duplicate Ownership Invariant

At any logical instant after successful fencing:

```text
only current owner may commit
```

workflow/task state transitions.

---

# 147. No Hidden Side Effect Invariant

Deterministic workflow execution must not silently perform external side effects.

---

# 148. Replay Invariant

Replay of identical history must produce identical workflow decisions.

---

# 149. Idempotency Invariant

Any operation exposed as retryable must explicitly define its idempotency semantics.

---

# 150. Cancellation Invariant

Cancellation must never be represented as automatic rollback of external effects.

---

# 151. Compensation Invariant

Compensation is an independent business operation and may fail.

---

# 152. Timer Invariant

Durable timers survive runtime process failure.

---

# 153. State Invariant

Workflow state must have a schema fingerprint.

---

# 154. Security Invariant

Workflow execution cannot acquire additional capabilities merely by scheduling an activity.

---

# 155. Resource Invariant

A workflow cannot bypass Resource Governor limits through retries or parallel branches.

---

# 156. Queue Invariant

An expired lease cannot authorize a stale worker to commit new state.

---

# 157. Version Invariant

Changing workflow source code cannot implicitly alter already-running workflow instances.

---

# 158. Storage Invariant

Workflow history must be durable before the runtime acknowledges a durable transition.

---

# 159. Ordering Invariant

Ordering guarantees are scoped and explicit.

The system never implies global ordering where none exists.

---

# 160. Failure Invariant

No failure path may silently convert:

```text
Failed
```

into:

```text
Completed
```

---

# 161. Resource Isolation Invariant

One tenant/workflow cannot consume unlimited queue, CPU, memory, network, or worker resources.

---

# 162. Deterministic Clock Invariant

Workflow time is obtained only through the workflow runtime.

---

# 163. Randomness Invariant

Workflow randomness must be deterministic or recorded.

---

# 164. Signal Invariant

Signals are durable before they are acknowledged.

---

# 165. Migration Invariant

Workflow migration must explicitly identify source and destination schema/version.

---

# 166. Security Boundary

```text
Workflow
   │
   ├── deterministic logic
   │
   └── Activity
          │
          └── Capability boundary
                │
                ├── Network
                ├── Storage
                ├── Device
                ├── Process
                └── External Service
```

This prevents workflow code from becoming an implicit privileged execution context.

# 171. Core Design Decisions

The following decisions are frozen for Axiom 629:

1. **Workflow execution is deterministic.**
2. **External side effects are activities.**
3. **At-least-once execution is the default.**
4. **Exactly-once global execution is not promised.**
5. **Idempotency and fencing provide safe effects.**
6. **Durable timers do not require persistent processes.**
7. **Workflow history is durable.**
8. **Snapshots bound replay cost.**
9. **Workflow versioning is explicit.**
10. **Compensation is not rollback.**
11. **Distributed workflows are not distributed ACID transactions.**
12. **627 owns distributed coordination.**
13. **628 owns distributed durable data.**
14. **626 owns network services.**
15. **607 owns local execution scheduling.**
16. **606 owns resource governance.**
17. **603 owns capability security.**
18. **602 owns diagnostics.**
19. **No cloud vendor is required.**
20. **No third-party workflow engine is required.**

```text
    memory >= 16 GiB
    feature = tensor_compute
```

---

# 48. GPU Affinity

If CPU execution communicates heavily with a GPU:

```text
prefer same NUMA node
prefer local PCIe topology
prefer local GPU memory
```

when 614 exposes topology.

---

# 49. CPU Topology

CPU requirements may include:

```text
cores
threads
architecture
instruction set
NUMA node
performance class
```

```text
cpu:
```

# 50. Heterogeneous Cluster

A cluster may contain:

```text
x86_64
arm64
RISC-V
GPU nodes
CPU-only nodes
high-memory nodes
```

# 51. Cross-Architecture Execution

A binary compiled for x86_64 cannot silently execute on arm64.

Possible strategies:

```text
native artifact
emulation provider
cross-compiled artifact
```

Emulation is never implicit unless explicitly configured.

# 52. Worker Software Version

Workers advertise:

```text
provider versions
compiler ABI
package versions
```

```text
CapabilityRequirement

CapabilityGrant
    what execution is allowed to use
```

# 55. Multi-Tenant Worker Pools

A worker pool may serve:

```text
tenant A

tenant C
```

```text
capabilities
priority
```

# 56. Dedicated Worker Pools

# 57. Shared Worker Pools

# 58. Worker Concurrency

Worker limits:


are enforced by 606.

# 59. Admission Control

Before dispatch:

```text

capability admission
worker admission
queue admission
policy admission
```

# 60. Overcommit

CPU overcommit may be allowed.

GPU memory and physical device exclusivity generally require hard admission.

# 61. Backpressure

When cluster capacity is exhausted:

```text
queue
    ↓
backpressure
```

rather than:

```text
unbounded remote execution
```

# 62. Queue Partitioning

Large worker pools use partitions.

Partition keys may be:

```text
tenant
workflow
queue
data locality
hardware class
```

---

# 63. Work Stealing

630 may use distributed work stealing for suitable fine-grained tasks.

It must not be used for tasks with:

```text
strict locality
exclusive resources
strong affinity
non-transferable device state
```

unless explicitly supported.

---

# 64. Push vs Pull

Two dispatch modes:

```text
Push:
scheduler → worker

Pull:
worker → queue
```

Default distributed architecture should prefer pull for scalable worker fleets.

Push remains available for latency-sensitive or dedicated pools.

---

# 65. Worker Pull

Worker requests:

```text
request_work(capabilities, resources)
```

Scheduler returns a compatible task.

This naturally accounts for worker availability.

---

# 66. Push Dispatch

Push is appropriate when:

```text
strict placement
low latency
dedicated worker
GPU reservation
data locality
```

requires explicit assignment.

---

# 67. Hybrid Dispatch

A cluster may combine:

```text
pull
+
placement reservation
+
worker affinity
```

This is the preferred flexible model.

---

# 68. Remote Procedure Execution

630 can expose:

```text
remote_call(
    target,
    function,
    input
)
```

but the operation must still obey:

```text
capabilities
timeouts
resource limits
serialization
versioning
fencing
```

---

# 69. Remote Function ABI

Remote functions use stable schema contracts.

```text
FunctionId
InputSchema
OutputSchema
Version
ABI
```

Serialization uses 612.

---

# 70. Remote Object Prohibition

630 does not expose arbitrary distributed object references by default.

Instead use:

```text
data references
service handles
workflow IDs
resource handles
```

This avoids hidden distributed pointer semantics.

---

# 71. No Distributed Pointer Model

Axiom explicitly avoids:

```text
remote_pointer
remote_reference
transparent_remote_object
```

because they hide:

- latency;
- failure;
- ownership;
- serialization;
- consistency.

---

# 72. Batch Compute

630 supports batch execution:

```text
map
batch
scatter
gather
reduce
```

Example:

```text

    encode(image)
```

The runtime may partition input across workers.

---

# 73. Map Execution

```text
InputSet
    ↓
Partition
    ↓
Workers
    ↓
PartialResults
```

# 74. Reduce Execution

```text
      /     \
    R1       R2
   / \       / \
  A   B     C   D
```

```text
ordering
associativity
precision
```

must be explicit.

# 76. Data-Parallel Compute

```text
partition 3 → worker 3
```

# 77. Streaming Compute

Tasks can process streams without materializing the entire dataset.

```text
source
  ↓
worker A
  ↓
worker B
  ↓
worker C
```

# 78. Pipeline Execution

A distributed pipeline may contain:

# 79. Pipeline Placement

```text
network transfer
serialization
device transfer
memory copies
```

while respecting resource constraints.

# 80. Zero-Copy Boundary

```text
GPU buffer

network buffer
```

can be transferred without copying.

# 81. Shared Memory

```text
intermediate artifacts
```

through 613.

# 86. Execution Reproducibility

# 87. Remote Execution Security

Before executing remote code:

```text
target compatible
```

where supported by platform capabilities.

# 90. Secret Propagation

may be resolved only at the execution boundary and only if the worker has the required capability.

# 91. Worker Isolation

Execution isolation may be:

```text
separate process
sandbox
VM
external service
```

# 93. Cluster Health

Health aggregates:

```text
resource pressure

coordination health
```

# 94. Pressure States


# 95. Worker Warmup

states.

through a provider.

```text
OS/Hardware
```

```text
 └── Node
      └── Worker
```

# 106. CPU Execution

```text
node
worker
```

```text
thread
task
core
local execution order
```

# 108. Device Loss

If a GPU/device is lost:

```text
execution → DeviceLost
```

```text
retry
migrate
fail
```

according to task policy.

---

# 109. Non-Idempotent Compute

A compute unit can declare:

```text
NonRetryable
```

# 110. Execution Uncertainty

When the network disconnects after a task may have completed:

```text
UnknownOutcome
```

is a valid state.

```text
Failed
```

or:

```text
Completed
```

without evidence.

# 111. Resolution of Unknown Outcome

```text
QueryWorker

ManualResolution
```

# 112. Deadline-Aware Scheduling

Tasks may have deadlines.

```text

transfer time
startup time
execution estimate
```

# 113. Deadline Does Not Guarantee Completion

A deadline is a policy constraint, not a guarantee.

---

# 114. Admission by Deadline

Possible outcomes:

```text
Accept
Queue
Reject
Escalate
```

---

# 115. Latency-Aware Placement

For interactive requests, placement can consider network RTT.

The runtime may prefer:

```text

```

without assuming geographic meaning.

---

# 116. Cost-Aware Placement

A provider may expose abstract execution cost.

```text

    cpu_cost
    memory_cost
    gpu_cost
    network_cost
```

---

# 117. Energy-Aware Placement

Embedded/mobile systems may expose:

```text
EnergyProfile
```

allowing preference for lower-energy execution.

---

# 118. Thermal-Aware Placement

614/606 may expose thermal pressure.

630 can reduce scheduling onto thermally constrained nodes.

---

# 119. Queue Fairness

Queue fairness policies:

```text
StrictPriority
WeightedFair
FIFO
Deadline
TenantFair
```

must be explicitly selected.

---

# 120. Preemption

Tasks can declare:

```text
Preemptible
NonPreemptible
Checkpointable
```

---

# 121. Preemption Safety

Preemption must not occur while a non-interruptible external side effect is executing unless the activity provider declares safe cancellation.

# 122. Graceful Preemption

Preferred sequence:

```text
checkpoint
    ↓
stop
    ↓
release resources
    ↓
reschedule
```

---

# 123. Hard Kill

Hard kill is a last-resort supervisor operation through 605.

The resulting task state is:

```text
ExecutionLost
```

unless completion was independently committed.

---

# 124. Distributed Batch Scheduling

Batch jobs can specify:

```text
parallelism
max_parallelism
min_parallelism
partition_size
```

---

# 125. Map/Reduce Failure

Failed partitions can be retried independently when deterministic/idempotent.

---

# 126. Straggler Handling

For suitable workloads:


may launch duplicate work.

---

# 127. Speculative Execution

A task may have:

```text
Attempt 1 → Worker A
Attempt 2 → Worker B
```

---

# 128. Duplicate Suppression

Every logical computation has:

```text

Attempt
```

# 129. Cluster Discovery

```text
Manual
```

No discovery mechanism is mandatory.

```text
register resources

Ready
```

```text
release leases
```

Upgrade process:

```text
new workers join

validate
        ↓
old workers drain

old workers leave
```

# 133. Version Compatibility

Workers and tasks must negotiate:

```text
protocol version
ABI
schema
compute artifact
provider capabilities
```

# 135. Remote Logging

```text
wrong architecture
```

# 139. Resource Reservation

```text
actual
```

so scheduling does not mistake reservations for actual usage.

The scheduler should consider fragmentation.

may not satisfy:

even though total free memory is 24 GiB.

# 143. NUMA Placement

When available:

```text
CPU
memory
GPU
PCIe
```

topology can be considered.

# 144. Memory Pressure

If a node becomes memory constrained:

according to policy.

---

# 145. Worker Quarantine


state.

---

# 146. Fault Domains

630 can distribute replicas/tasks across:

```text
Node
Rack
Zone
Region
```

according to topology metadata.

---

# 147. No Global Cluster Lock

```text
local queues
atomic counters
leases
sharded state
```

# 148. Scheduler Partitioning

```text
tenant
queue

```

# 149. Coordinator Failure

```text

 ↓
new owner
 ↓
fence old owner
 ↓
```

---

# 150. Persistent Scheduling State

The minimal durable state includes:

```text
assignment
lease
fence token
attempt
```

```text
leases
```

from authoritative sources.

```text
Completed
Failed

Lost
```

```text
model
```


```text

same device
```

---

# 209. Session Affinity


to keep state on one worker.

The session can later migrate only if state migration is supported.

---

```text
Checkpointable
Persistent
```

---

```text
611
612
628
```

---

# 212. Worker Restart

---

# 213. Model Warmup

# 241. Architecture Invariants

1. A worker cannot self-authorize capabilities.
2. A stale worker cannot commit authoritative results.
3. A stale scheduler cannot own a partition after fencing.
4. Hard placement constraints cannot be ignored.
5. Soft placement preferences cannot override security.
6. Resource reservations expire.
7. Worker leases expire.
8. Remote pointers are not part of the core model.
9. Large data is represented by references where practical.
10. Execution identity is distinct from task identity.
11. Attempt identity is distinct from logical task identity.
12. Unknown execution outcome is a valid state.
13. Exactly-once execution is not promised.
14. Idempotent effects are encouraged.
15. Non-idempotent tasks require explicit retry policy.
16. Remote code must be verified.
17. Capability requirements do not grant capabilities.
18. Worker crash does not imply task failure if outcome is unknown.
19. Resource accounting is delegated to 606.
20. Local scheduling is delegated to 607.
21. Distributed coordination is delegated to 627.
22. Distributed data placement is delegated to 628.
23. Network transport is delegated to 626/609.
24. Process supervision is delegated to 605.
25. Device ownership is delegated to 614.
26. Long-running business orchestration is delegated to 629.
27. Arbitrary native code cannot be transparently migrated.
28. Checkpointability must be declared.
29. Deterministic computation may be cached only when explicitly eligible.
30. Security policy changes cannot silently grant authority.
31. A resource snapshot may be stale.
32. Placement is a decision, not a completion guarantee.
33. Admission failure must be observable.
34. Backpressure must be bounded.
35. Scheduler hot paths must avoid a global lock.
36. Cluster topology is abstract.
37. Cloud APIs are not required.
38. Worker state is not automatically persistent.
39. Persistent data belongs to storage layers.
40. Cluster recovery must be able to reconstruct authoritative execution state.
41. Duplicate execution must be safely detectable.
42. Result commits require valid execution authority.
43. Queue fairness must be explicit.
44. Preemption requires declared safety.
45. Device loss must produce explicit execution state.
46. Cross-cluster execution requires explicit trust.
47. Capability lifetime must be bounded.
48. Resource policy cannot be bypassed through task fan-out.
49. Large task graphs must not require O(all workers) placement scans.
50. Minimal profiles must dead-strip unused distributed compute functionality.

# 1. Purpose

BOOTSTRAP-631 defines the native Axiom runtime for applications composed of multiple cooperating services.

It provides:

- service identity;
- service registration;
- service discovery;
- endpoint management;
- service instances;
- health-aware routing;
- client-side load balancing;
- server-side request admission;
- connection management;
- request routing;
- retries;
- timeout/deadline propagation;
- circuit breakers;
- bulkheads;
- request hedging;
- locality-aware routing;
- service version routing;
- traffic policies;
- weighted routing;
- failover;
- graceful service draining;
- service-to-service authentication;
- capability-aware calls;
- distributed tracing;
- service dependency visibility;
- service topology diagnostics.

631 sits above raw networking and distributed compute.

# 2. Fundamental Separation

Axiom explicitly distinguishes:

```text
Service
ServiceInstance
Endpoint
Process
Worker
Task
Workflow
```

Definitions:

```text
Service
    logical network-accessible capability

ServiceInstance
    concrete running instance of a service

Endpoint
    concrete reachable network address

Process
    OS execution unit

Worker
    compute execution provider

Task
    executable unit of work

Workflow
    durable orchestration
```

Therefore:

```text
Service != Process
Service != Worker
Service != Workflow
```

# 219. Architecture Invariants

1. Service identity is distinct from endpoint identity.
2. Service identity is distinct from process identity.
3. Endpoint availability does not imply authorization.
4. Discovery is not authorization.
5. Health is not identity.
6. Liveness is not readiness.
7. A draining instance receives no new traffic.
8. Expired service leases cannot receive authoritative traffic.
9. Routing cannot grant capabilities.
10. Downstream capability must be attenuated.
11. Retry is never universally automatic.
12. Non-idempotent uncertain operations are not blindly retried.
13. Request deadlines propagate downstream.
14. Retry budgets are bounded.

16. Circuit breakers are local routing state.
17. Outlier ejection does not rewrite authoritative health.
18. Soft routing preferences cannot override hard requirements.
19. Security policy cannot be bypassed by local fast paths.

21. IPC optimization must preserve authorization semantics.
22. Cached discovery must respect expiration.
23. Cached authorization must respect revocation.
24. Large responses should be referenceable.
25. Service state required for recovery must be persisted explicitly.
26. Sticky sessions are not persistence.
27. Sidecar is optional.
28. Cloud infrastructure is optional.
29. HTTP is optional.
30. A global registry is optional.
31. A service mesh is optional.
32. A service cannot silently escalate worker capabilities.
33. Routing policies are declarative.
34. Arbitrary routing scripts are not part of the hot path.
35. Connection pools are resource-governed.
36. Backpressure is bounded.
37. Load shedding is explicit.
38. Unknown outcome is a valid state.
39. Service contract versions are explicit.
40. Breaking API changes require versioning.
41. Service discovery does not imply service startup.
42. Service activation is delegated to 605.
43. Distributed coordination is delegated to 627.
44. Distributed data is delegated to 628.
45. Remote execution is delegated to 630.
46. Transport is delegated to 626/609.
47. Cryptography is delegated to 610.

49. Local execution is delegated to 607.

# 220. Architecture Invariants

1. Gateway is an edge policy runtime.
2. Gateway is not the service registry.
3. Gateway is not the distributed coordinator.
4. Gateway is not the cryptographic primitive provider.
5. Gateway is not the service implementation.
6. Gateway never grants authority.
7. Gateway may attenuate authority.
8. Authentication precedes protected execution.
9. Authorization precedes protected execution.
10. Client-supplied identity is untrusted by default.
11. Route selection is deterministic.
12. Configuration activation is atomic.
13. Invalid configuration does not partially activate.
14. Request deadlines propagate.
15. Retry budgets are bounded.
16. Non-idempotent operations are not blindly retried.
17. Hedging requires explicit safety.
18. Circuit breakers fail fast when open.
19. Rate limits are bounded.
20. Request queues are bounded.
21. Connection pools are resource-governed.
22. Response caches respect authorization boundaries.
23. Static resources obey filesystem capabilities.
24. Egress destinations require policy.
25. SSRF protection is mandatory for unrestricted URL inputs.
26. Header spoofing is prevented at trust boundaries.
27. TLS credentials use secure storage.
28. Secret values are excluded from ordinary telemetry.
29. Gateway shutdown drains active work.
30. Long-lived streams have explicit limits.
31. Sidecars are optional.
32. Service mesh is optional.
33. Cloud infrastructure is optional.
34. HTTP/3 is optional.
35. Distributed state is optional unless policy requires it.
36. Local fast paths preserve security semantics.
37. Protocol adapters preserve gateway policy semantics.
38. No arbitrary hot-path scripting is required.
39. No mandatory GC exists.
40. Unused features must be dead-strippable.

**BOOTSTRAP-632 — COMPLETE**

# BOOTSTRAP-633
## Native Distributed API Contract, Schema Registry, RPC IDL, Code Generation, Client/Server Stubs, Compatibility Checking & Service SDK Runtime 5.0

**Status:** COMPLETE  
**Layer:** Distributed API / Contract / SDK Runtime  
**Depends on:** BOOTSTRAP-600 → BOOTSTRAP-632

---

# 1. Purpose

BOOTSTRAP-633 defines the native Axiom contract system for distributed APIs.

Its purpose is to make communication between:

- clients;
- servers;
- services;
- gateways;
- workers;
- applications;
- external integrations

strongly typed, versioned, inspectable, and independently evolvable.

The central principle is:

```text
API Contract
    ↓
Schema
    ↓
Generated Client / Server
    ↓
Transport
    ↓
Runtime
```

The application developer should not need to manually construct protocol frames, serialize every field, validate every request, or maintain duplicated client/server definitions.

---

# 2. Architectural Position

```text

                         │
                         ▼
                 ┌───────────────┐
                 │ API Contract  │
                 │     633       │
                 └───────┬───────┘
                         │
              ┌──────────┼──────────┐
              ▼          ▼          ▼
          Client SDK   Server SDK   Schema
              │          │           │
              └──────┬───┴───────────┘
                     ▼
              626 / 631 / 632
                     │
              609 / 604 / 610
                     │
                  Network
```

A contract describes:

```text

types
errors
streaming
compatibility
security requirements
timeouts
idempotency
```

It does not describe:

```text
internal algorithms
memory layout
database implementation
thread implementation
private state
```

A malicious schema cannot cause unbounded compiler or decoder work.

---

# 149. Compiler Integration

Compiler phases:

```text
parse
 ↓
contract analysis
 ↓
schema lowering
 ↓
compatibility validation
 ↓
code generation
 ↓
IR
 ↓
native compilation
```

---

# 150. IR Representation

IR may contain:

```text
ContractRef
OperationRef
Encode
Decode
Validate
Call
StreamOpen
StreamSend
StreamReceive
StreamClose
```

---

# 151. Optimization

Compiler can:

```text
inline small encoders
eliminate unused fields
specialize serializers
remove unused operations
remove unused transports
```

---

# 152. Dead Stripping

An application using one operation should not automatically link every generated service.

---

# 153. Reflection

Runtime reflection is not required.

Compile-time contract metadata is preferred.

---

# 154. Runtime Introspection

Optional metadata package can provide:

```text
service list
operation list
schema
version
fingerprint
```

---

# 155. AI-Readable Metadata

Generated `.axapi` should contain:

```text
purpose
types
operations
constraints
security
errors
compatibility
examples
```

in deterministic machine-readable form.

---

# 156. Documentation Generation

Tooling can generate:

```text
HTML
Markdown
JSON
Axiom metadata
```

from contracts.

---

# 157. API Explorer

Optional GUI/CLI can inspect contracts without requiring the service to execute arbitrary code.

---

# 158. CLI

Canonical commands:

```text
ax api inspect
ax api validate
ax api check
ax api generate
ax api diff
ax api publish
ax api fetch
ax api docs
```

---

# 159. API Diff

Example:

```text
ax api diff old.axapi new.axapi
```

reports field, operation, error, security and transport changes.

---

# 160. Compatibility CI

Build systems can fail when a declared compatibility policy is violated.

---

# 161. Compatibility Policy

Projects can choose:

```text
BackwardOnly
ForwardOnly
Bidirectional
WireOnly
Strict
```

---

# 162. Version Pinning

Production clients can pin:

```text
ContractFingerprint
```

instead of relying solely on semantic versions.

---

# 163. Version Range

Development clients may accept:

```text
>=1.2 <2.0
```

when compatibility rules permit.

---

# 164. Service Upgrade

A service can expose multiple contract versions simultaneously.

---

# 165. Contract Routing

631/632 can select an implementation based on contract/version.

---

# 166. Graceful Migration

Typical migration:

```text
v1 client
   ↓
gateway
   ↓
v1 server

v2 client
   ↓
gateway
   ↓
v2 server
```

---

# 167. Adapter Contract

Explicit adapters may translate:

```text
v1 request
→
v2 request
```

but must be declared and tested.

---

# 168. No Silent Semantic Translation

The runtime must not assume that a structurally compatible change is semantically equivalent.

---

# 169. Generated Test Client

Compiler tooling can generate test clients for every operation.

---

# 170. Contract Test Server

A generated conformance server validates:

```text
encoding
decoding
validation
errors
streaming
```

without implementing business logic.

---

# 171. Golden Tests

Wire representations can be stored as deterministic golden fixtures.

---

# 172. Fuzz Testing

Generated decoders must support fuzz testing.

---

# 173. Differential Testing

Two implementations of the same contract can be compared against identical generated requests.

---

# 174. Property Tests

Properties include:

```text
encode → decode ≈ identity
unknown fields do not corrupt known fields
invalid input never escapes decoder
```

---

# 175. Transport Tests

The same contract test suite should run over:

```text
IPC
TCP
TLS
HTTP
AxiomRPC
```

where providers exist.

---

# 176. Failure Tests

Test:

```text
timeout
disconnect
partial response
malformed response
server restart
contract mismatch
authentication failure
```

---

# 177. Deterministic Testing

A virtual transport and deterministic scheduler allow reproducible distributed API tests.

---

# 178. Mock Provider

A test provider can replace actual transport.

---

# 179. Fake Server

Generated fake servers can verify client behavior without network access.

---

# 180. Contract-Based Mocking

Mocks are generated from contracts rather than manually maintained interfaces.

---

# 181. Performance Model

Target characteristics:

```text
low allocation
bounded serialization overhead
zero-copy where possible
connection reuse
compile-time validation
```

---

# 182. Small API Optimization

Small request/response objects should avoid unnecessary heap allocation.

---

# 183. Large Payload Optimization

Large payloads should use:

```text
streaming
views
chunked buffers
zero-copy
```

where practical.

---

# 184. Batch Serialization

Repeated homogeneous messages may use batch encoders.

---

# 185. CPU Affinity

Serialization work may be scheduled through 607/606.

---

# 186. Resource Accounting

Every transport call can charge:

```text
CPU
memory
network bytes
connections
streams
```

to the appropriate scope.

---

# 187. Quotas

API contracts can carry descriptive quota metadata.

Enforcement remains in 606/631/632.

---

# 188. Observability

Generated clients and servers emit:

```text
operation name
contract fingerprint
latency
status
retry count
bytes
```

without exposing secrets.

---

# 189. Trace Naming

Canonical span naming:

```text
Service.Operation
```

with stable identifiers available for machine analysis.

---

# 190. Metrics Cardinality

Unbounded user data must never automatically become metric labels.

---

# 191. Logging

Generated runtime errors include:

```text
request_id
operation_id
contract_fingerprint
```

where safe.

---

# 192. Configuration

Default client/server behavior is configurable through 601.

---

# 193. Security Policy

Contract requirements cannot weaken application-level security policy.

Runtime policy may strengthen restrictions.

---

# 194. Package Registry Integration

625 can publish:

```text
contract
generated SDK
compatibility metadata
documentation
```

as package artifacts.

---

# 195. Dependency Resolution

A client package may declare:

```text
requires api UserService >=1.2 <2
```

and resolve a compatible contract.

---

# 196. Offline Builds

All generated code must be reproducible offline when contract artifacts are available locally.

---

# 197. Reproducibility

Generated artifacts should be independent of:

```text
machine path
wall-clock time
randomness
```

unless explicitly requested.

---

# 198. Source Mapping

Generated code maintains mapping back to:

```text
contract
operation
field
```

for diagnostics.

---

# 199. IDE Integration

Tooling can provide:

```text
go to operation
go to schema
find consumers
find implementations
show compatibility
generate client
```

---

# 200. AI Integration

AI tooling can consume `.axapi` without parsing implementation code.

The contract metadata becomes the authoritative public API description.

---

# 201. API Change Analysis

AI/compiler tooling can identify:

```text
affected clients
affected servers
breaking changes
security changes
transport changes
```

without generating a subjective overall score.

---

# 202. Service SDK

The generated SDK may contain:

```text
Client
Server
Types
Errors
Validators
Serializers
Transport adapters
Documentation metadata
Tests
```

---

# 203. SDK Profiles

```text
ClientOnly
ServerOnly
ClientServer
TypesOnly
SchemaOnly
Interop
```

---

# 204. Minimal Client

A small application using one unary operation should be able to link only:

```text
schema
encoder
decoder
transport
operation
```

rather than the complete SDK.

---

# 205. Minimal Server

Similarly, unused client-side facilities must be removable from server binaries.

---

# 206. Interop SDK

External languages may receive generated:

```text
C ABI
JSON schema
OpenAPI
```

artifacts.

---

# 207. Native Axiom Preference

Axiom-to-Axiom communication uses native contract representation by default.

---

# 208. External Compatibility

External protocol support must not distort the native contract model.

---

# 209. Final Contract Flow

```text
                     .axapi
                       │
                 ┌─────▼─────┐
                 │   Schema  │
                 │ Registry  │
                 └─────┬─────┘
                       │
             ┌─────────┴─────────┐
             ▼                   ▼
       Generated Client    Generated Server
             │                   │
             ▼                   ▼
          626/631             626/631
             │                   │
             └─────────┬─────────┘
                       ▼
                    609/604
                       │
                    Network
```

---

# 210. Architecture Invariants

1. Contract identity is deterministic.
2. Contract fingerprints are canonical.
3. Field IDs are stable.
4. Removed field IDs cannot be silently reused.
5. Wire schema is independent from native memory layout.
6. Source compatibility and wire compatibility are distinct.
7. Security compatibility is independently checked.
8. Unknown fields are handled explicitly.
9. Unknown enum values cannot corrupt execution.
10. Unknown variants are safely represented.
11. Contract versions are immutable once published.
12. Registry is optional.
13. Centralized registry is not required at runtime.
14. Generated code is deterministic.
15. Generated code is statically typed.
16. Reflection is optional.
17. Runtime code generation is not required.
18. Client cannot manufacture capabilities.
19. Authentication context is separate from business payload.
20. Secret fields are excluded from ordinary telemetry.
21. Decoder resource usage is bounded.
22. Streaming has explicit backpressure.
23. Cancellation propagates.
24. Deadlines propagate.
25. Retry behavior is bounded.
26. Non-idempotent calls are not blindly retried.
27. Transport is replaceable.
28. IPC and network transports share contract semantics.
29. Gateway does not redefine contract identity.
30. Service discovery and contract discovery remain separate.
31. Compatibility checking is deterministic.
32. Breaking changes are explicit.
33. Semantic equivalence is never inferred solely from structure.
34. Generated adapters preserve security requirements.
35. Generated clients do not bypass authorization.
36. Generated servers verify contract implementation.
37. Generated schemas are fuzz-testable.
38. Generated wire formats are deterministic where canonical encoding is requested.
39. No mandatory GC exists.
40. Unused SDK features are dead-strippable.

---

# 211. Acceptance Criteria

The implementation must demonstrate at least:

### Contract
- service definitions;
- operation definitions;
- stable IDs;
- versioning;
- fingerprints;
- canonicalization;
- typed errors;
- streaming contracts;
- security metadata.

### Schema
- structs;
- enums;
- unions;
- options;
- results;
- collections;
- optional fields;

- validation;

### Generation
- client generation;
- server generation;
- serializer generation;
- decoder generation;
- validator generation;
- documentation generation;
- test generation;
- deterministic output.

### Runtime
- unary RPC;
- server streaming;
- client streaming;
- bidirectional streaming;
- cancellation;
- deadline propagation;
- connection pooling;
- load balancing;
- retries;
- typed errors.

### Compatibility
- backward compatibility checks;
- forward compatibility checks;
- wire compatibility;
- ABI compatibility;
- security compatibility;
- breaking-change diagnostics;
- version ranges;
- fingerprint pinning.

### Registry
- local registry;
- package registry;
- remote registry provider;
- signed schemas;
- immutable versions;
- offline cache;
- schema discovery.

### Security
- authentication metadata;
- authorization metadata;
- capability requirements;
- secret-field classification;
- bounded decoding;
- malformed-schema protection;
- credential propagation;
- no capability escalation.

### Integration
- 604 IPC;
- 609 networking;
- 610 cryptography;
- 612 serialization;
- 625 package registry;
- 626 application protocols;

### Tooling
- `ax api inspect`;

- `ax api check`;
- `ax api generate`;
- `ax api diff`;
- `ax api publish`;
- `ax api fetch`;
- `ax api docs`.

### Testing
- golden wire tests;
- fuzzing;
- property testing;
- differential testing;
- transport conformance;
- deterministic virtual transport;
- timeout tests;
- cancellation tests;
- compatibility tests;
- security tests.

**Target: ≥250 acceptance criteria.**

---

Axiom now has a complete contract path:

Tiếp tục với **BOOTSTRAP-634**.

:::writing{variant="document" id="85217" title="BOOTSTRAP-634 — Native Distributed Event Bus, Pub/Sub, Message Broker Boundary, Topic Partitioning, Consumer Groups, Delivery Guarantees & Stream Processing Runtime 5.0"}

# BOOTSTRAP-634
## Native Distributed Event Bus, Pub/Sub, Message Broker Boundary, Topic Partitioning, Consumer Groups, Delivery Guarantees & Stream Processing Runtime 5.0

**Status:** COMPLETE  
**Layer:** Distributed Event / Messaging / Stream Runtime  
**Depends on:** BOOTSTRAP-600 → BOOTSTRAP-633

---

# 1. Purpose

BOOTSTRAP-634 defines the native Axiom runtime for distributed event-driven applications.

It provides:

- publish/subscribe;
- distributed topics;
- partitions;
- consumer groups;
- durable event streams;
- transient event streams;
- message delivery;
- acknowledgements;
- retries;
- dead-letter queues;
- ordering;
- replay;
- offsets;
- event retention;
- compaction;
- stream processing;
- filtering;
- transformation;
- windowing;
- aggregation;
- joins;
- checkpointing;
- backpressure;
- event routing;
- event schema management;
- distributed event observability.

The runtime is designed to work without requiring Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, Pulsar, Redis Streams, or another mandatory external broker.

External brokers are provider adapters.

---

# 2. Architectural Position

```text
                         PRODUCER
                            │
                            ▼
                    ┌───────────────┐
                    │     634       │
                    │ EVENT RUNTIME │
                    ├───────────────┤
                    │ Topics        │
                    │ Partitions    │
                    │ Log           │
                    │ Routing       │
                    │ ConsumerGroup │
                    │ Delivery      │
                    │ Retry/DLQ    │
                    │ Stream Proc. │
                    └───────┬───────┘
                            │
                ┌───────────┼───────────┐
                ▼           ▼           ▼
             Consumer A  Consumer B  Processor
                            │
                            ▼
                          628
```

---

# 3. Relationship With BOOTSTRAP-628

628 defines distributed data replication and event-log primitives.

634 builds the application-facing event distribution model above those primitives.

```text
628
 = replicated data/log foundation

634
 = event distribution + consumer semantics + stream processing
```

---

# 4. Relationship With BOOTSTRAP-629

629 handles durable workflows and jobs.

634 provides the event trigger and event transport used by workflows.

```text
634 Event
   ↓
629 Workflow
   ↓
Activities
```

---

# 5. Relationship With BOOTSTRAP-633

633 defines event schemas.

634 transports and processes instances of those schemas.

---

# 6. Event Model

An event consists of:

```text
EventId
EventType
SchemaFingerprint
ProducerId
Timestamp
PartitionKey
Headers
Payload
```

---

# 7. Event Identity

Each event has a globally unique logical identity when durable identity is required.

The identity must not depend on consumer attempts.

---

# 8. Event Sequence

Within a partition:

```text
PartitionOffset
```

provides a monotonic sequence.

Offsets are scoped to the partition.

---

# 9. Topic

```text
Topic:
    TopicId
    Name
    SchemaPolicy
    RetentionPolicy
    PartitionPolicy
    DeliveryPolicy
    SecurityPolicy
```

---

# 10. Topic Identity

A topic has a stable:

```text
TopicId
```

independent of its human-readable name.

---

# 11. Topic Naming

Topic names use canonical UTF-8 identifiers.

Names must not contain ambiguous normalization variants.

---

# 12. Topic Namespace

Namespaces can separate:

```text
application
tenant
environment
organization
system
```

---

# 13. Topic Lifecycle

```text
Created
 ↓
Active
 ↓
Draining
 ↓
Archived
 ↓
Deleted
```

---

# 14. Topic Creation

Creation requires authorization.

Applications cannot create arbitrary topics without the corresponding capability.

---

# 15. Topic Configuration

Configuration includes:

```text
partitions
replication
retention
maximum message size
ordering
compression
encryption
consumer policy
```

---

# 16. Partition

A topic consists of one or more partitions.

```text
Topic
 ├── Partition 0
 ├── Partition 1
 ├── Partition 2
 └── ...
```

---

# 17. Partition Identity

```text
PartitionId =
    TopicId + PartitionNumber + Generation
```

---

# 18. Partition Ordering

Events within one partition have a strict append order.

Cross-partition global ordering is not guaranteed.

---

# 19. Partition Key

Producer can provide:

```text
PartitionKey
```

to preserve related events in the same partition.

---

# 20. Partition Selection

Default selection:

```text
hash(PartitionKey) % partition_count
```

A configurable deterministic partitioner may be used.

---

# 21. No Ordering Illusion

A system must never claim total ordering merely because multiple partitions are consumed sequentially by one client.

---

# 22. Partition Rebalancing

Changing partition count may alter key distribution.

The runtime must explicitly distinguish:

```text
PartitionExpansion
```

from ordinary consumer rebalancing.

---

# 23. Stable Key Ordering

Applications requiring stable per-key ordering should use a partition strategy that preserves key-to-partition mapping.

---

# 24. Producer

```text
Producer:
    ProducerId
    Topic
    Policy
```

---

# 25. Publish API

```text
fn Producer.publish(
    event: Event
) -> Future<Result<PublishReceipt>>
```

---

# 26. Batch Publish

```text
fn Producer.publish_batch(
    events: EventBatch
) -> Future<Result<BatchPublishReceipt>>
```

---

# 27. Publish Receipt

Contains:

```text
EventId
TopicId
PartitionId
Offset
Timestamp
```

---

# 28. Acknowledgement

Publish acknowledgement levels:

```text
None
Accepted
Persisted
Replicated
Committed
```

---

# 29. Delivery Guarantees

Supported semantics:

```text
AtMostOnce
AtLeastOnce
EffectivelyOnce
```

The runtime does not claim magical distributed exactly-once semantics.

---

# 30. At-Most-Once

Event is delivered at most once but may be lost.

---

# 31. At-Least-Once

Event may be delivered multiple times.

Consumers must support idempotency where required.

---

# 32. Effectively-Once

Achieved through:

```text
stable EventId
deduplication
idempotent consumer
transactional state update
```

rather than relying on an unrestricted global exactly-once transaction.

---

# 33. Consumer

```text
Consumer:
    ConsumerId
    Topic
    Subscription
```

---

# 34. Consumer Group

A consumer group allows multiple consumers to share partitions.

```text
Topic
 ├── P0 → Consumer A
 ├── P1 → Consumer B
 └── P2 → Consumer C
```

---

# 35. Consumer Group Identity

```text
ConsumerGroupId
```

is independent of individual process identity.

---

# 36. Group Membership

Each member has:

```text
MemberId
Generation
Capabilities
Health
Lease
```

---

# 37. Rebalancing

When membership changes:

```text
join
leave
failure
capacity change
```

partitions may be reassigned.

---

# 38. Rebalance Generation

Every assignment has a generation.

Stale consumers cannot commit offsets against a newer generation unless explicitly permitted.

---

# 39. Assignment Strategies

```text
Range
RoundRobin
Sticky
Cooperative
LoadAware
LocalityAware
```

---

# 40. Cooperative Rebalancing

Preferred where supported to minimize unnecessary partition movement.

---

# 41. Partition Affinity

Consumers may express:

```text
zone
region
device
GPU
CPU architecture
data locality
```

preferences.

---

# 42. Consumer Poll

```text
fn Consumer.poll(
    max_events: usize,
    deadline: Deadline
) -> Future<Result<EventBatch>>
```

---

# 43. Push Subscription

Optional provider mode:

```text
subscribe(callback)
```

must still obey bounded concurrency and backpressure.

---

# 44. Pull Preferred Core

The canonical core consumer model uses pull semantics because they provide explicit flow control.

---

# 45. Offset

A consumer tracks:

```text
Topic
Partition
Offset
```

---

# 46. Offset Commit

```text
fn Consumer.commit(
    offset: Offset
) -> Result<void>
```

---

# 47. Commit Semantics

The runtime must distinguish:

```text
received
processed
side_effect_completed
committed
```

---

# 48. Safe Commit Rule

For at-least-once processing:

```text
process
 ↓
durable side effect
 ↓
commit offset
```

is the default safe sequence.

---

# 49. Auto Commit

Auto-commit is optional and must never be presented as equivalent to processing acknowledgement.

---

# 50. Offset Store

Offsets may be stored in:

```text
local
628 distributed store
durable log
external provider
```

---

# 51. Offset Retention

Offset history may have retention independent from event retention.

---

# 52. Start Position

Consumer can start:

```text
Earliest
Latest
Timestamp
Offset
EventId
Snapshot
```

---

# 53. Replay

Consumers can intentionally replay historical events.

---

# 54. Replay Isolation

Replay must not accidentally modify production state unless explicitly configured.

---

# 55. Replay Mode

```text
Live
Replay
CatchUp
ReplayThenLive
```

---

# 56. Consumer Pause

A consumer can pause consumption while preserving assignment and/or lease within configured limits.

---

# 57. Consumer Resume

Resume starts from the last valid committed or explicitly selected position.

---

# 58. Backpressure

Consumers advertise capacity:

```text
max events
max bytes
max concurrent processing
```

---

# 59. Producer Backpressure

A topic can reject or delay publishing when:

```text
storage pressure
replication lag
partition overload
quota exhaustion
```

occurs.

---

# 60. Bounded Queues

No mandatory internal queue may grow without a configured bound.

---

# 61. Event Size

Topic policies define:

```text
max event bytes
max header bytes
max batch bytes
```

---

# 62. Event Headers

Headers are typed metadata:

```text
name
type
value
```

---

# 63. Header Security

Sensitive headers can be marked:

```text
Secret
Internal
```

and excluded from telemetry.

---

# 64. Event Schema

Every typed event may reference:

```text
SchemaFingerprint
```

from 633.

---

# 65. Schema Validation

Producer can validate before publish.

Consumer must not assume producers are trustworthy.

---

# 66. Consumer Validation

A consumer may reject incompatible schemas before decoding payloads.

---

# 67. Schema Evolution

Events follow 633 compatibility rules.

---

# 68. Schema Registry

634 can resolve schema metadata from 633.

---

# 69. Schema Cache

Frequently used schemas should be cached locally.

---

# 70. Schema Mismatch

A consumer receiving an incompatible schema produces a typed:

```text
SchemaMismatch
```

error.

---

# 71. Dead-Letter Queue

Failed events can be redirected to:

```text
DLQ
```

with failure metadata.

---

# 72. DLQ Event

A dead-letter record contains:

```text
OriginalEvent
FailureReason
FailureCount
FirstFailure
LastFailure
ConsumerId
ConsumerGeneration
```

---

# 73. Retry Queue

Retry scheduling can use:

```text
Immediate
Delayed
ExponentialBackoff
FixedDelay
Calendar
```

---

# 74. Retry Budget

Retries are bounded by:

```text
max attempts
max elapsed time
max bytes
```

---

# 75. Retry Storm Prevention

Backoff uses bounded exponential delay plus jitter.

---

# 76. Poison Event

An event repeatedly failing deterministic validation should not remain indefinitely in the primary queue.

---

# 77. Poison Handling

Policy:

```text
Retry
Quarantine
DLQ
Skip
StopPartition
StopConsumer
```

---

# 78. Partition Stop

Stopping one partition must not automatically stop unrelated partitions.

---

# 79. Event Ordering With Retry

A topic can choose:

```text
StrictPartitionOrder
BestEffortOrder
```

---

# 80. Strict Ordering

A failed event blocks later events in the same partition until policy resolves it.

---

# 81. Best-Effort Ordering

Failed events may be delayed or redirected while later events continue.

---

# 82. Event Retention

Retention can be:

```text
TimeBased
SizeBased
CountBased
Compacted
UntilAcknowledged
Manual
```

---

# 83. Time-Based Retention

Events older than the configured retention period become eligible for reclamation.

---

# 84. Size-Based Retention

Partition storage is bounded by configured capacity.

---

# 85. Compaction

Compaction may retain the latest value per logical key.

---

# 86. Compaction Safety

Compaction is valid only when topic semantics declare the key/value model.

---

# 87. Tombstones

Compacted topics can represent deletion using tombstone records.

---

# 88. Tombstone Retention

Tombstones must remain long enough to prevent stale replicas from resurrecting deleted state.

---

# 89. Event Log

Each durable partition is an append-oriented log.

---

# 90. Segment

A partition log is divided into segments for:

```text
storage
retention
compaction
recovery
```

---

# 91. Segment Index

Indexes support efficient lookup by:

```text
offset
timestamp
event ID
```

---

# 92. Checksum

where explicitly configured.

# 236. External Broker Providers

Optional adapters:

```text
KafkaProvider
NatsProvider
RabbitMqProvider
PulsarProvider
RedisStreamProvider
CloudEventProvider
```

These are interoperability modules, not core dependencies.

---

# 237. Provider Contract

All providers implement the common event semantics as far as the underlying system permits.

---

# 238. Semantic Gaps

If an external provider cannot provide a requested guarantee, the runtime must report the limitation rather than silently pretending the guarantee exists.

---

# 239. Cloud Provider Boundary

Cloud-managed queues/event buses are optional providers.

---

# 240. Local Embedded Bus

A small-process event bus should be available without networking.

---

# 241. In-Process Fast Path

For same-process producers and consumers:

```text
publish
 ↓
lock-free/bounded queue
 ↓
consumer
```

may bypass serialization while preserving contract semantics.

---

# 242. Same-Node IPC

604 may provide the next-level fast path.

---

# 243. Cross-Process Semantics

The same EventId/schema/security semantics must survive IPC transport.

---

# 244. Cross-Service Semantics

631/626 can carry the same event contract across services.

---

# 245. Gateway Integration

632 may expose event submission APIs such as:

```text
POST /events/UserCreated
```

mapped to 634 topics.

---

# 246. Authentication

Gateway-authenticated identity becomes producer context only through explicit policy.

---

# 247. Event API Rate Limiting

632/606 can limit:

```text
events/sec
bytes/sec
batch size
```

at the external boundary.

---

# 248. Administrative API

Administrative operations include:

```text
list topics
inspect topic
list partitions
inspect consumer group
inspect lag
pause consumer
resume consumer
replay
purge
inspect schema
inspect stream
```

---

# 249. Dangerous Operations

Operations such as:

```text
purge
truncate
rewind
force-leader
delete-topic
```

require elevated capability.

---

# 250. Audit

Administrative event operations generate 602 audit records.

---

# 251. Security Invariants

1. Publish requires authorization.
2. Subscribe requires authorization.
3. Consumer-group access is separately controlled.
4. Topic administration requires elevated capability.
5. Cross-tenant subscription requires explicit authorization.
6. Payloads are not automatically trusted.
7. Event headers are not automatically trusted.
8. Secret fields are excluded from ordinary telemetry.
9. External broker providers cannot silently elevate capabilities.
10. Replay cannot bypass authorization.

---

# 252. Performance Invariants

1. Local publish must avoid unnecessary serialization.
2. Consumer queues are bounded.
3. Partition processing is parallelizable.
4. Stateful operators preserve key affinity.
5. Hot paths avoid global locks.
6. Buffer reuse is supported.
7. Large events can stream.
8. Batch operations are supported.
9. Dead features are removable.
10. No GC is mandatory.

---

# 253. Reliability Invariants

1. Partition ordering is explicit.
2. Offset generation prevents stale commits.
3. Lease expiry fences stale consumers.
4. Retries are bounded.
5. DLQ prevents poison-event loops.
6. Checkpoints are durable where configured.
7. Recovery replays from a known position.
8. Replication uses fencing.
9. Split-brain writes are prevented.
10. Data-loss semantics are explicit.

---

# 254. Stream-Processing Invariants

1. Operator graphs are typed.
2. Unbounded state requires explicit policy.
3. Windows have explicit retention.
4. Late events have explicit handling.
5. Checkpoints identify input offsets.
6. State schema is versioned.
7. State migration is explicit.
8. External side effects are explicit.
9. Replay semantics are deterministic where promised.
10. Backpressure propagates.

---

# 255. Acceptance Criteria

The implementation must demonstrate at least:

### Event Bus
- topic creation;
- topic deletion;
- topic metadata;
- partitions;
- partition offsets;
- publish;
- batch publish;
- event IDs;
- event headers;
- schema references.

### Consumer
- consumer groups;
- membership;
- leases;
- partition assignment;
- rebalance;
- offset commit;
- replay;
- pause/resume;
- cooperative shutdown.

### Delivery
- at-most-once;
- at-least-once;
- deduplication;
- retry;
- delayed retry;
- retry budgets;
- DLQ;
- poison-event handling.

### Ordering
- partition ordering;
- keyed ordering;
- strict ordering;
- best-effort ordering;
- partition affinity.

### Storage
- durable log;
- retention;
- compaction;
- tombstones;
- segment indexing;
- checksums;
- compression;
- encryption;
- replication.

### Stream Processing
- map;
- filter;
- key-by;
- merge;
- split;
- window;
- aggregation;
- join;
- repartition;
- stateful operator;
- checkpoint;
- recovery;
- replay;
- state migration.

### Security
- producer capabilities;
- consumer capabilities;
- topic administration;
- tenant isolation;
- encrypted transport;
- encrypted storage;
- secret metadata;
- audit.

### Integration
- 600 state/checkpoint;
- 601 configuration;
- 602 diagnostics;
- 603 capabilities;
- 604 IPC;
- 605 supervision;
- 606 resources;
- 607 async;
- 608 synchronization;
- 609 networking;
- 610 cryptography;
- 611 storage;
- 612 serialization;
- 613 compression/package;
- 625 distribution;
- 628 distributed data;
- 629 workflows;
- 630 distributed compute;
- 631 services;
- 632 gateway;
- 633 API contracts.

### Testing
- deterministic event bus;
- deterministic scheduler;
- partition failure;
- broker failure;
- consumer crash;
- duplicate delivery;
- rebalance;
- stale commit;
- retry storm;
- poison event;
- schema mismatch;
- state recovery;
- late event;
- watermark;
- stream upgrade;
- state migration;
- fuzzing.

**Target: ≥300 acceptance criteria.**

---

# 256. Runtime Profiles

```text
AXEVENT_NONE
    no event runtime

AXEVENT_LOCAL
    in-process event bus

AXEVENT_IPC
    local distributed-process messaging

AXEVENT_DURABLE
    durable event log

AXEVENT_PUBSUB
    distributed pub/sub

AXEVENT_STREAM
    stream processing

AXEVENT_REPLICATED
    replicated event infrastructure

AXEVENT_EXTERNAL
    external broker providers

AXEVENT_FULL
    complete event platform
```

---

# 257. Final Architecture

```text
                         PRODUCERS
                            │
                            ▼
                    ┌────────────────┐
                    │      634       │
                    │ EVENT RUNTIME  │
                    ├────────────────┤
                    │ Auth / Policy  │
                    │ Topics         │
                    │ Partitions     │
                    │ Durable Log    │
                    │ Replication    │
                    │ Consumer Group │
                    │ Offset Store   │
                    │ Retry / DLQ    │
                    │ Pub/Sub        │
                    │ Stream Engine  │
                    │ Checkpoints    │
                    └───────┬────────┘
                            │
             ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
             ▼              ▼              ▼
         Consumer       Workflow       Stream Sink
             │              │              │
             ▼              ▼              ▼
            629            628            611
             │
             ▼
            630

         ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Foundations                       │
         │ 603 Security                      │
         │ 606 Resources                     │
         │ 607 Scheduler                     │
         │ 608 Synchronization               │
         │ 610 Crypto                        │
         │ 612 Serialization                 │
         │ 633 Contracts                     │
         └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

# 258. Completion

**BOOTSTRAP-634 — COMPLETE**

Axiom now has a complete distributed event path:

```text
633 Contract
      ↓
634 Event Bus
      ↓
Topic / Partition
      ↓
Consumer Group
      ↓
Stream Processor
      ↓
628 State / 629 Workflow / 630 Compute / 631 Service
```

This establishes the event-driven backbone needed for large distributed Axiom applications while keeping broker implementations replaceable.

**NEXT TASK: BOOTSTRAP-635 — Native Distributed Scheduler, Cluster Membership, Leader Election, Consensus Boundary, Placement, Service Coordination & Control-Plane Runtime 5.0**

parts:
Tiếp tục chuỗi đặc tả Axiom. Task kế tiếp là **BOOTSTRAP-635**, xây lớp control-plane phân tán làm nền cho scheduler, cluster, leader election, placement và coordination.

:::writing{variant="document" id="58321" title="AXIOM BOOTSTRAP-635 — Native Distributed Scheduler, Cluster Membership, Leader Election, Consensus Boundary, Placement, Service Coordination & Control-Plane Runtime 5.0"}
# BOOTSTRAP-635
# Native Distributed Scheduler, Cluster Membership, Leader Election, Consensus Boundary, Placement, Service Coordination & Control-Plane Runtime 5.0

**Status:** COMPLETE  
**Layer:** Distributed Control Plane / Cluster Runtime  
**Depends on:** BOOTSTRAP-600 → BOOTSTRAP-634  
**Primary dependencies:** 603, 605, 606, 607, 608, 610, 611, 612, 628, 629, 630, 631, 632, 633, 634

---

## 1. Mục tiêu

BOOTSTRAP-635 định nghĩa control-plane phân tán native của Axiom.

Nó cung cấp:

- cluster membership;
- node identity;
- node health và failure detection;
- topology;
- cluster epochs/generations;
- leader election;
- consensus boundary;
- replicated control state;
- distributed leases;
- fencing;
- distributed coordination;
- workload placement;
- resource-aware scheduling;
- service coordination;
- reconciliation;
- node draining;
- workload evacuation;
- rescheduling;
- rolling coordination;
- maintenance coordination;
- cluster-level policy;
- multi-node control-plane APIs.

635 **không biến Axiom thành Kubernetes**.

Axiom chỉ cung cấp primitive runtime native đủ để xây dựng:

- cluster runtime;
- service platform;
- distributed compute;
- event processing;
- workflow workers;
- deployment controllers;
- database clusters;
- edge clusters;
- private infrastructure;
- embedded distributed systems.

External systems có thể được tích hợp thông qua provider boundary.

---

# 2. Nguyên tắc kiến trúc

## 2.1 Control plane ≠ data plane

635 quản lý:

```text
membership
leadership
desired state
placement
coordination
leases
control state
```

Không trực tiếp xử lý:

```text
application payload
large data streams
media streams
user traffic
bulk storage
GPU tensors
```

Các workload này thuộc:

- 609/626 networking;
- 628 distributed data;
- 629 workflow;
- 630 distributed compute;
- 631 service runtime;
- 632 gateway;
- 634 event runtime.

---

## 2.2 Không bắt buộc Kubernetes

Không có dependency bắt buộc vào:

- Kubernetes;
- etcd;
- Consul;
- ZooKeeper;
- Nomad;
- Raft implementation;
- cloud control plane.

Các hệ thống trên chỉ có thể xuất hiện dưới dạng provider/adapter.

---

## 2.3 Consensus là boundary

Axiom định nghĩa semantics của consensus nhưng không ép một thuật toán duy nhất.

```text
ConsensusProvider
```

có thể được implement bằng:

```text
Raft
Multi-Paxos
BFT provider
External consensus service
Platform consensus
Single-node deterministic provider
```

Core runtime chỉ yêu cầu các invariant về:

- term;
- quorum;
- commit;
- ordering;
- fencing;
- membership;
- leader safety.

---

## 2.4 Không có "best effort" đối với safety-critical control state

Control state quan trọng phải có semantics rõ ràng:

```text
Committed
Uncommitted
Applied
Stale
Unknown
```

Không được coi:

```text
locally observed
```

là:

```text
globally committed
```

---

# 3. Cluster Model

Cluster là tập hợp các node cùng tham gia một control domain.

```text
Cluster
 ├── ClusterId
 ├── ClusterGeneration
 ├── Membership
 ├── Topology
 ├── ControlState
 ├── Leader
 ├── Scheduler
 └── Coordination
```

---

# 4. Core Identity Types

```text
ClusterId
NodeId
NodeGeneration
ClusterGeneration

LeaderId
LeaderTerm

WorkloadId
WorkloadGeneration

PlacementId
LeaseId
FencingToken

ControlRevision
```

Tất cả identity phải có generation/revision khi cần tránh ABA.

---

# 5. Node Identity

Một node được định danh bởi:

```text
NodeIdentity {
    node_id
    node_generation
    cluster_id
    boot_id
    build_id
    platform
    architecture
}
```

`NodeId` không được tái sử dụng đồng thời cho hai generation.

---

# 6. Node Lifecycle

Node states:

```text
Joining
Ready
Suspect
Unhealthy
Draining
Leaving
Failed
Quarantined
Removed
```

State transition:

```text
Joining
   ↓
Ready
   ↓
Suspect
   ↓
Unhealthy
   ↓
Failed
```

Node có thể quay lại:

```text
Suspect → Ready
```

nếu failure detector xác nhận hồi phục.

---

# 7. Node Generation

Mỗi lần node boot lại phải tạo:

```text
NodeGeneration++
```

Ví dụ:

```text
node-A / generation 41
```

khác hoàn toàn:

```text
node-A / generation 42
```

Mọi lease/assignment/control record phụ thuộc node phải có generation.

Điều này ngăn:

```text
old node
```

tiếp tục thực hiện hành động sau reboot.

---

# 8. Cluster Generation

Cluster membership configuration có:

```text
ClusterGeneration
```

Mọi thay đổi membership quan trọng tạo revision mới.

Ví dụ:

```text
generation 100
generation 101
generation 102
```

Không được áp dụng membership configuration cũ nếu revision thấp hơn revision hiện tại.

---

# 9. Membership Provider

```text
trait MembershipProvider {
    join(...)
    leave(...)
    observe(...)
    list(...)
    watch(...)
}
```

Provider có thể là:

```text
StaticMembership
SeedMembership
GossipMembership
ConsensusMembership
ExternalMembership
EmbeddedMembership
```

---

# 10. Membership Lease

Node phải duy trì membership lease.

```text
MembershipLease {
    node_id
    node_generation
    lease_id
    expires_at
    renewal_revision
}
```

Node mất khả năng renew không lập tức đồng nghĩa node chết.

Nó chuyển qua:

```text
Suspect
```

sau đó mới:

```text
Unhealthy
Failed
```

theo failure detector policy.

---

# 11. Heartbeat

Heartbeat có:

```text
Heartbeat {
    node_id
    generation
    sequence
    monotonic_time
    health_summary
    resource_summary
    control_revision
}
```

Heartbeat không được sử dụng làm nguồn duy nhất cho consensus safety.

---

# 12. Failure Detector

Failure detector phải phân biệt:

```text
Healthy
Suspected
Unreachable
Failed
Unknown
```

Failure detector có thể sử dụng:

- heartbeat;
- direct probes;
- indirect probes;
- network reachability;
- process supervision;
- OS health;
- resource pressure;
- application health;
- consensus observation.

Không được suy ra:

```text
network timeout == process definitely dead
```

---

# 13. Split-Brain Protection

Axiom phải bảo vệ control-plane khỏi stale node.

Cơ chế:

```text
Term
Epoch
Generation
Lease
FencingToken
ConsensusCommit
```

Một node cũ có thể vẫn đang chạy nhưng không còn authority.

Ví dụ:

```text
Leader A term=51
    ↓ partition

Cluster elects B term=52
    ↓

A must no longer mutate protected state.
```

---

# 14. Topology

Node có topology metadata:

```text
region
zone
rack
host
room
datacenter
network_domain
failure_domain
power_domain
gpu_domain
storage_domain
```

Ví dụ:

```text
NodeTopology {
    region = "vn"
    zone = "hn-1"
    rack = "r07"
    gpu = "cuda"
    storage = "nvme"
}
```

Topology là metadata, không phải assumption cứng của scheduler.

---

# 15. Node Labels

Node có labels:

```text
label("gpu", "a100")
label("arch", "x86_64")
label("storage", "nvme")
label("zone", "hn-1")
```

Labels phải:

- typed hoặc canonical string;
- deterministic;
- versioned;
- bounded;
- policy-controlled.

---

# 16. Node Taints

Node có thể khai báo:

```text
Taint {
    key
    value
    effect
}
```

Effects:

```text
PreferNoSchedule
NoSchedule
NoExecute
```

Workload cần explicit toleration nếu muốn chạy trên node bị taint.

---

# 17. Resource Advertisement

Node công bố:

```text
CPU
Memory
GPU
VRAM
Storage
IOPS
Network
Threads
Handles
IPC
Device
```

Resource accounting sử dụng semantics của BOOTSTRAP-606.

Không được duy trì một resource accounting system thứ hai.

---

# 18. Node Capacity

```text
NodeCapacity {
    total
    allocatable
    reserved
    used
    available
}
```

Phải phân biệt:

```text
physical capacity
reserved capacity
allocatable capacity
currently free capacity
```

---

# 19. Workload Model

```text
Workload {
    workload_id
    generation
    desired_state
    resource_request
    placement_policy
    security_policy
    runtime_policy
}
```

Workload có thể đại diện cho:

```text
service
worker
workflow activity
compute task
event processor
gateway instance
database replica
custom process
```

---

# 20. Desired State

Ví dụ:

```text
Service A
desired_instances = 8
```

Control plane không trực tiếp đảm bảo 8 instance tồn tại.

Nó duy trì:

```text
desired = 8
actual = 6
```

và reconciliation sẽ tạo thêm 2.

---

# 21. Actual State

Actual state đến từ:

- supervisor 605;
- service runtime 631;
- compute runtime 630;
- workflow runtime 629;
- event runtime 634;
- node membership;
- health providers.

---

# 22. Reconciliation Loop

Control plane thực hiện:

```text
observe
→ compare
→ plan
→ validate
→ commit
→ execute
→ observe
```

Không được:

```text
mutate desired state
```

chỉ để che giấu actual-state failure.

---

# 23. Reconciler

```text
trait Reconciler<T> {
    observe(...)
    diff(...)
    plan(...)
    validate(...)
    apply(...)
}
```

`plan()` phải có thể chạy deterministic trong cùng input state.

---

# 24. Reconciliation Safety

Một reconciliation operation phải kiểm tra:

```text
object generation
cluster generation
leader term
resource availability
security policy
capabilities
fencing token
```

trước mutation.

---

# 25. Scheduler

Scheduler là control-plane component tạo placement decisions.

```text
Scheduler
 ├── Filter
 ├── Score
 ├── Reserve
 ├── Commit
 └── Reconcile
```

---

# 26. Scheduling Pipeline

```text
Workload
 ↓
Admission
 ↓
Constraint filtering
 ↓
Resource filtering
 ↓
Security filtering
 ↓
Topology filtering
 ↓
Scoring
 ↓
Reservation
 ↓
Placement commit
 ↓
Execution
```

---

# 27. Placement

```text
Placement {
    placement_id
    workload_id
    node_id
    node_generation
    resources
    fencing_token
    revision
}
```

Placement luôn gắn với node generation.

---

# 28. Hard Constraints

Hard constraints có thể gồm:

```text
required capability
required architecture
required GPU
minimum memory
required zone
required device
required security profile
required package
required network domain
```

Không thỏa hard constraint → node bị loại.

---

# 29. Soft Constraints

Soft constraints:

```text
locality
spread
latency
cost metadata
cache locality
data locality
GPU locality
network locality
```

Chỉ dùng để scoring.

---

# 30. Affinity

Workload có thể yêu cầu:

```text
Affinity {
    workload
    service
    node
    topology
    data
    device
}
```

---

# 31. Anti-Affinity

Ví dụ:

```text
replica A ≠ same node as replica B
```

hoặc:

```text
replicas should spread across zones
```

Anti-affinity có thể là:

```text
Hard
Preferred
```

---

# 32. Spreading

Scheduler hỗ trợ spread theo:

```text
node
rack
zone
region
failure domain
power domain
```

Mục tiêu là tránh concentration.

---

# 33. Bin Packing

Provider scheduler có thể sử dụng:

```text
BestFit
FirstFit
WorstFit
BalancedFit
ResourceAwareFit
```

Đây là algorithm choices, không phải ranking của scheduler.

---

# 34. Scoring Provider

```text
trait PlacementScorer {
    score(workload, node, context) -> Score
}
```

Score phải:

- bounded;
- deterministic trong cùng input;
- không thay đổi security semantics;
- không cấp thêm capability.

---

# 35. Locality

Scheduler có thể ưu tiên:

```text
data locality
cache locality
GPU locality
network locality
storage locality
```

nhưng locality không được vượt qua hard security constraints.

---

# 36. GPU Placement

GPU placement tích hợp 614/630.

Hỗ trợ:

```text
GPU count
GPU memory
GPU type
compute capability
device partition
exclusive GPU
shared GPU
accelerator class
```

---

# 37. Device Affinity

Workload có thể yêu cầu:

```text
device = GPU
device = camera
device = FPGA
device = NIC
device = accelerator
```

Device capability phải được cấp qua 603.

---

# 38. Reservation

Scheduler có thể reserve resources trước khi commit.

```text
Reservation {
    reservation_id
    workload_id
    node_id
    resources
    expires_at
}
```

Reservation hết hạn tự động giải phóng.

---

# 39. Reservation Atomicity

Nếu placement yêu cầu nhiều resource:

```text
CPU
Memory
GPU
Storage
```

scheduler không được commit partial reservation.

Hoặc:

```text
all reserved
```

hoặc:

```text
none reserved
```

---

# 40. Preemption

Preemption là optional policy.

Có thể:

```text
NoPreemption
BestEffort
PriorityBased
QuotaAware
```

Preemption phải:

- kiểm tra capability;
- tôn trọng workload protection;
- tạo audit event;
- có grace period;
- tránh starvation.

---

# 41. Priority

Priority là scheduling property.

Priority không được bypass:

- security;
- tenancy isolation;
- hard resource limit;
- capability policy;
- node taint.

---

# 42. Fairness

Scheduler phải hỗ trợ:

```text
tenant fairness
workload fairness
resource fairness
priority fairness
```

Không được để một tenant monopolize cluster nếu policy không cho phép.

---

# 43. Tenant Quota

Quota lấy semantics từ 606.

Ví dụ:

```text
tenant-A:
    cpu <= 32
    memory <= 128GiB
    gpu <= 2
```

Scheduler không tự tạo quota system riêng.

---

# 44. Scheduler Queue

Scheduler có:

```text
Pending
Admitted
Scheduled
Blocked
Rejected
```

Queue phải bounded hoặc quota-controlled.

---

# 45. Scheduling Backpressure

Khi scheduler quá tải:

```text
admission control
queue limit
tenant quota
priority
load shedding
```

Không được để pending workloads tăng vô hạn.

---

# 46. Leader Election

Cluster control-plane có leader abstraction:

```text
Leader
Term
Lease
Election
```

# 247. Safety Properties

Các invariant bắt buộc:

1. stale leader cannot commit;
2. stale node generation cannot own new placement;
3. fencing token monotonically protects resource;
4. committed state is never treated as uncommitted;
5. uncommitted state is never treated as committed;
6. security constraints cannot be bypassed by scheduler scoring;
7. hard constraints cannot be overridden by soft preferences;
8. quota cannot be bypassed through placement;
9. duplicate command cannot create duplicate committed mutation;
10. expired lease cannot authorize protected mutation.

---

# 248. Additional Safety Invariants

11. at most one valid leader per term;
12. lower term cannot supersede higher term;
13. lower generation cannot supersede higher generation;
14. old placement cannot activate;
15. stale observation cannot overwrite newer observation;
16. control state machine is deterministic;
17. reconciliation is idempotent;
18. fencing is checked at mutation boundary;
19. node quarantine blocks protected operations;
20. control credentials never enter ordinary telemetry.

---

# 249. More Invariants

21. consensus provider is replaceable;
22. scheduler provider cannot alter security authority;
23. data plane cannot become control-plane authority implicitly;
24. event bus cannot substitute for consensus;
25. workload cannot grant cluster capability to itself;
26. resource accounting comes from 606;
27. device identity comes from 614;
28. service execution comes from 631;
29. process execution comes from 605;
30. distributed data authority comes from 628.

### Placement
- [ ] Placement có generation.

- [ ] Duplicate activation bị ngăn.
- [ ] Failed activation được recovery.
- [ ] Node drain hoạt động.
- [ ] Node evacuation hoạt động.
- [ ] Failed-node rescheduling hoạt động.
- [ ] Anti-thrashing hoạt động.

### Reconciliation
- [ ] Reconciler deterministic.
- [ ] Reconciler idempotent.
- [ ] Stale observation không overwrite state mới.
- [ ] Desired/actual convergence có kiểm thử.

### Integration
- [ ] 605 integration.
- [ ] 606 integration.

### Security

# 301. Final Design Decision

BOOTSTRAP-635 xác lập **Axiom Distributed Control Plane** theo nguyên tắc:

```text

    +
Consensus
    +

    +

```

là một runtime native độc lập.

Nó **không yêu cầu Kubernetes**, không ép Raft, không ép cloud provider và không biến scheduler thành một execution engine.

Boundary quan trọng nhất:

```text
635 decides
605 executes processes
631 executes services
629 executes workflows
630 executes distributed compute
634 transports events
628 stores distributed state
606 accounts resources
603 authorizes authority
633 observes the system
```

Điều này giữ cho Axiom có một control-plane đủ mạnh để xây dựng hệ thống phân tán lớn nhưng vẫn giữ được khả năng compile/dead-strip xuống một runtime rất nhỏ khi ứng dụng không cần distributed features.

# BOOTSTRAP-637
## Native Distributed Configuration, Feature Flags, Dynamic Policy, Runtime Experimentation, Progressive Delivery Signals & Global Control Registry Runtime 5.0

**Status:** COMPLETE  
**Layer:** Distributed Dynamic Control Plane  
**Depends on:** BOOTSTRAP-600 through BOOTSTRAP-636  
**Primary dependencies:** 601, 603, 628, 631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636

---

# 1. Mục tiêu

BOOTSTRAP-637 bổ sung một runtime native cho phép hệ thống Axiom thay đổi **behavior runtime** mà không cần rebuild hoặc redeploy binary.

Nó cung cấp:

- distributed configuration;
- runtime configuration;
- feature flags;
- kill switches;
- dynamic operational policies;
- experimentation;
- deterministic targeting;
- progressive-delivery signals;
- configuration rollout;
- configuration rollback;
- global control registry;
- federation-aware configuration;
- edge/offline configuration;
- configuration watches;
- configuration snapshots;
- revision history;
- drift detection;
- safe fallback.

637 **không** phải:

- local configuration system;
- secret manager;
- service discovery;
- deployment controller;
- security capability engine;
- arbitrary remote scripting engine.

Ranh giới:

```text
601  Local Application Configuration
       │
       ▼
637  Distributed Dynamic Control
       │
       ├── Configuration
       ├── Feature Flags
       ├── Runtime Policy
       ├── Experiments
       ├── Progressive Signals
       └── Global Control Registry
       │
       ├──────────────► 631 Service Runtime
       ├──────────────► 632 Gateway
       ├──────────────► 633 Telemetry
       ├──────────────► 634 Event Runtime
       └──────────────► 636 Deployment
```

---

# 2. Thiết kế nền tảng

637 sử dụng nguyên tắc:

> **Dynamic data, static code.**

Remote control có thể thay đổi dữ liệu điều khiển nhưng không được thay đổi executable semantics tùy ý.

Ví dụ hợp lệ:

```text
request_timeout = 3000ms
cache_ttl = 60s
feature_x = true
max_connections = 500
sampling_rate = 0.05
traffic_weight = 10%
```

Không hợp lệ:

```text
execute(remote_code)
load(remote_script)
eval(remote_expression_with_side_effects)
```

637 không tạo remote-code-execution primitive.

---

# 3. Phân biệt các hệ thống liên quan

| Hệ thống | Trách nhiệm |
|---|---|
| 601 | configuration local/bootstrap |
| 603 | security capability/policy |
| 628 | distributed replicated state |
| 631 | service discovery/routing |
| 633 | telemetry |
| 634 | event distribution |
| 635 | cluster control/consensus |
| 636 | deployment/rollout |
| 637 | runtime dynamic control |

Đặc biệt:

```text
601 = "ứng dụng được cấu hình như thế nào khi khởi động?"

637 = "ứng dụng đang được điều khiển như thế nào khi đang chạy?"
```

---

# 4. Architecture

637 gồm các tầng:

```text

                    │      Axiom Applications       │
                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │
                          Typed Runtime API
                                    │

                    │       Config Runtime          │
                    ├───────────────────────────────┤
                    │ Feature Flag Runtime           │
                    │ Experiment Runtime             │
                    │ Dynamic Policy Runtime         │
                    │ Progressive Signal Runtime     │
                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │
                    ┌───────────────▼───────────────┐
                    │    Snapshot / Watch Layer      │
                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │
                    ┌───────────────▼───────────────┐
                    │   Distributed Control Store    │
                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │
               ┌────────────────────┼───────────────────┐

             628                  635                 Edge
        Replicated Data       Control Plane        Federation
```
